project.name: Al Kazhnah Leather Factory — ISO 27001 & TISAX Delivery
project.description: End-to-end ISO/IEC 27001:2022 + TISAX (VDA ISA 6.0, AL2, Information Security module, target ML3) implementation for Al Kazhnah Leather Factory. ALL delivery work — full technical implementation, ISMS documentation, internal audit, corrective actions, readiness — completes by Wed 2026-09-30 (start Mon 2026-07-27). CB and ENX audit-provider bookings made by 2026-08-12 so external audits land at the earliest possible dates: ISO Stage 1 ~Sep 29, TISAX AL2 ~Oct 7, Stage 2 ~Oct 28, certificate + labels by late Nov (Phase 6 tail, assessor-calendar dependent). Team: Manoj (lead), Masha.

modules.name: Phase 1 — Gap Assessment & Verification of Existing State
Phase 4 — Awareness, Internal Audit & Management Review

issues.name: Hold kickoff workshop and confirm project charter
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Run a half-day kickoff with Al Kazhnah leadership on day one or two. Manoj presents the 17-week delivery plan, phase gates, and the delivery rule: everything claimed as implemented is verified before documentation, and every gap is remediated inside the window. Make explicit that the engagement runs through the assessments: Phase 6 (2026-11-23 to 2027-01-29) hosts ISO Stage 1, Stage 2 and the TISAX AL2 assessment, ending with certificate and ENX labels in hand. Frame leadership obligations against ISO 27001 clause 5.1.

Masha organises logistics, scribes, and captures the RACI. Secure named counterparts for six roles — sponsor, ISMS owner, IT lead, HR, facilities, procurement — and include the production manager: TISAX fieldwork reaches the shop floor, so plan around shift patterns and flag the possible Mawlid holiday (late August) and UAE National Day (early December).

Close by confirming client obligations (counterpart availability, procurement budget, ENX and certification-body fees are client-paid), the escalation path, the weekly Friday call (W1-W17) and the fortnightly assessment-window check-ins (A1-A4). Present the charter for sponsor sign-off in-session or within 24 hours.

### Inputs

- Signed engagement contract and proposal scope
- Draft charter and RACI from Underwings house templates
- Leadership availability confirmed for a half-day slot on 27-28 July

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed project charter filed in the evidence repository under `00-project`
- RACI matrix naming all six client counterparts
- Kickoff minutes and attendance list, filed same day

### Acceptance criteria

- Sponsor acknowledges the charter in writing
- All six counterpart roles have a named person with contact details
- Minutes and attendance filed in the evidence repository
- Weekly call slot and escalation path agreed and recorded

issues.name: Define and document ISMS scope statement (clause 4.3)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Draft the ISMS scope statement per ISO 27001 clause 4.3: covered sites (factory and offices, with addresses), organisational units, business processes (leather production and supply to automotive customers), information systems, network boundaries and interfaces, plus justified exclusions. Manoj drafts after kickoff, walks the physical and network boundary with the client IT lead, and reviews with the sponsor.

Write the text so it can be pasted verbatim into the ENX portal as the TISAX scope description — ISO and TISAX scopes must stay congruent, and the TISAX scope must include every location where automotive-customer protected information is handled, including remote work. Keep it tight: an over-broad scope inflates both audits, an under-scoped one voids the label's value to the customer.

Hand a stable draft of the scope text to Masha by 29 July so P0.4 registration is not blocked; finalise v1.0 by 31 July.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (charter, named counterparts, sponsor access)
- Org chart, site details and network diagram from P0.8 (drafts acceptable)
- House scope-statement template

### Outputs / Evidence

- ISMS scope statement v1.0, sponsor-approved, filed under the clause-4 folder of the evidence repository (structure from P0.6)
- Reusable scope text block handed to P0.4 for ENX entry

### Acceptance criteria

- Scope covers sites, units, processes, systems, boundaries and justified exclusions
- Sponsor approves v1.0 in writing
- Identical scope text entered in the ENX registration (P0.4)

issues.name: Record confirmed TISAX objective: AL2, IS module, target ML3
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Write a one-page TISAX scoping memo that locks the confirmed assessment objective: Assessment Level 2 (AL2), Information Security module only, protection need high, target maturity level 3 under VDA ISA 6.0. State explicitly what is excluded — the prototype protection and data protection modules, and AL3 — so later scope drift is refused with a document rather than an argument.

Manoj drafts; attach the automotive customer's TISAX request (e-mail or portal requirement) as the business driver — the assessor and the customer both expect the objective to trace to a real requirement. Use ENX participant-handbook terminology so the memo matches what P0.4 enters in the portal, and note that AL2 means a plausibility check of the self-assessment with evidence, which raises the bar on evidence quality captured through Phases 1-3.

Walk the sponsor through the memo and obtain countersignature — this is a client decision with fee and effort consequences, not a consultant assumption.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (charter, sponsor availability)
- The automotive customer's TISAX request or contractual security requirement
- Draft scope text from P0.2 for consistency
- VDA ISA 6.0 catalogue and ENX participant handbook

### Outputs / Evidence

- Countersigned scoping memo filed under `00-project` in the evidence repository
- Customer TISAX request attached as an appendix
- Objective parameters recorded for reuse in P0.4 and P1.7

### Acceptance criteria

- Memo states AL2, IS module only, protection need high, target ML3, with exclusions
- Customer request attached
- Sponsor countersignature obtained and filed

issues.name: Register Al Kazhnah as TISAX participant on ENX portal
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Register Al Kazhnah as a TISAX participant on the ENX portal. Masha drives the mechanics with the client: create the participant account under the client's legal entity (never Underwings), enter legal, billing and location data exactly as on the trade licence, paste the scope text from P0.2, set the assessment objective from P0.3, and have client finance pay the participation fee.

This is the engagement's best-known lag item — ENX processing and fee settlement can take days to weeks, and the TISAX assessment cannot be booked (P5.3) without a participant ID. Start by day 3 at the latest, confirm who in the client can legally sign, and pre-warn finance that an ENX invoice is coming so it does not sit in an approval queue. UAE tip: pay by corporate card if permitted — international bank transfers add clearing days.

Track status daily and report at the W1 Friday call; escalate to the sponsor immediately if account validation or payment stalls.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.2 (scope text block) and P0.3 (assessment objective)
- Client legal-entity details, trade licence, billing data and authorised signatory
- Client finance contact briefed to pay the ENX fee
- Named client e-mail address to own the portal account

### Outputs / Evidence

- ENX participant account owned by the client, credentials held client-side
- Participant ID and scope ID recorded in the tracker and evidence repository
- Fee payment confirmation filed

### Acceptance criteria

- Registration submitted with scope text identical to P0.2
- Fee paid, or payment scheduled with evidence
- Participant ID issued, or the delay escalated at the W1 call with a dated follow-up

issues.name: Build stakeholder map, contact sheet and communication plan
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Build the stakeholder register and the communication plan the engagement runs on. Masha compiles internal stakeholders from the P0.1 RACI (sponsor, ISMS owner, IT lead, HR, facilities, procurement, production management) and adds external parties: the automotive customer's security contact, key IT suppliers, and placeholders for the certification body and TISAX audit provider selected in Phase 5.

Record role, interest, contact details, preferred channel and required touchpoints per stakeholder. Then write the one-page comms plan: the weekly Friday status call (W1-W9) with standing agenda, the escalation route to the sponsor with response times, the document approval flow (who signs policies at P2.15), and the shared channel for day-to-day exchange and evidence requests. In a factory, state how shop-floor staff are reached — supervisors and noticeboards, not e-mail — which P4.2 awareness delivery will depend on.

Manoj reviews for completeness; share the final version with the sponsor so client-side expectations are set in week one.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (RACI, counterpart names, agreed call slot)
- Client org chart from P0.8 (draft acceptable)
- House stakeholder-register and comms-plan templates

### Outputs / Evidence

- Stakeholder register and contact sheet filed under `00-project`
- Communication plan covering call cadence, escalation, approvals and shared channel
- Distribution note showing the sponsor received both

### Acceptance criteria

- All P0.1 counterpart roles plus external parties listed with contact details
- Comms plan reviewed by Manoj
- Both documents shared with the sponsor

issues.name: Set up evidence repository and document-control structure
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Stand up the evidence repository before fieldwork produces artifacts — retrofitting filing mid-engagement loses evidence. Masha creates a folder taxonomy keyed three ways: ISO 27001 clauses 4-10, Annex A themes A.5-A.8, and VDA ISA 6.0 chapters 1-5, plus a `00-project` area for charter, minutes and plans. One artifact, one home; the dual-mapped tracker (P0.7) carries cross-references, so never duplicate files across framework folders.

Define naming and version conventions in a one-page readme: document ID, short title, version, date, owner, status (draft, review, approved). Set access so both consultants and the named client ISMS owner can read and write, and confirm the repository lives where the client keeps it after handover — auditors will ask the client, not Underwings, to produce evidence.

Prove it works end-to-end: file a test document, revise it to v2, and have a client counterpart retrieve the current version unaided. The structure is formalised later by the document control procedure (P2.14) and becomes the backbone of P1.8, P3.15 and the P5.7 handover pack.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (named ISMS owner and IT lead for access setup)
- Client-approved storage platform with access granted to both consultants
- House folder-taxonomy and naming-convention templates

### Outputs / Evidence

- Live repository with clause, Annex A theme and ISA chapter taxonomy
- Naming and versioning readme filed at the repository root
- Access list showing consultants plus the client ISMS owner

### Acceptance criteria

- Test document filed, versioned and retrieved by a client counterpart
- Taxonomy covers clauses 4-10, themes A.5-A.8 and ISA chapters 1-5
- Conventions documented and applied to all files created so far

issues.name: Build dual-mapped control tracker (Annex A 93 <-> VDA ISA 6.0)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Build the dual-mapped control tracker — the single source of truth that lets one engagement serve two frameworks. Masha creates one row per ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control (all 93) and maps each to its VDA ISA 6.0 requirement(s), starting from a published mapping reference. Where mapping is partial or absent — some ISA requirements, notably the high-protection extras, have no clean Annex A twin — add ISA-only rows so nothing scored in P1.7 goes untracked.

Columns per row: control ID and title, mapped ISA requirement(s), exists (claimed), verified-by — Manoj's name only, nobody else signs this column — evidence link into the P0.6 repository, gap or remediation task reference, SoA applicability with justification, and ISA maturity current versus target ML3.

This covers all 93 controls without one-task-per-control noise: Phase 1 verification (P1.3-P1.7) fills the rows, P1.10 reads gaps from them, P2.7 derives the SoA, P3.15 links evidence packs, P3.16 re-scores. Manoj reviews mapping completeness row by row before Phase 1 relies on it — settle disputes now, not during the audit.

### Inputs

- ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control list and VDA ISA 6.0 catalogue
- Published Annex A to VDA ISA mapping reference
- Repository structure from P0.6 for evidence-link conventions

### Outputs / Evidence

- Control tracker v1.0 stored at the repository root with edit history enabled
- Mapping-exceptions note covering ISA-only and unmapped rows

### Acceptance criteria

- All 93 Annex A rows present, each with an ISA mapping or a documented exception
- ISA-only requirements captured as additional rows
- Columns include verified-by, evidence link, gap task, SoA and maturity current plus target
- Manoj has reviewed and approved mapping completeness

issues.name: Collect baseline client inputs (org chart, asset lists, network diagram)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Issue a structured baseline-information request to the client and drive it to completion — Phase 1 fieldwork quality depends on it. Masha compiles the request list from the house template: org chart, HR roster with roles, IT asset lists (servers, endpoints, network gear, software and licences), network diagram, supplier list with contracts, all existing security policies and procedures, prior audit or assessment reports, and any customer security requirements.

Send the list within 24 hours of kickoff with a named owner and due date per item, routed through the P0.1 counterparts. Track every item in a request log (requested, chased, received, filed) and chase daily, copying the sponsor per the P0.5 escalation route once an item ages past two days. Factory reality: expect the asset list and network diagram to be outdated or missing; accept imperfect versions now and note the deficiency, since P1.3 and P1.9 will verify and rebuild them anyway.

File everything received into the P0.6 repository under `01-client-inputs`, marking provenance and date — these are claimed-state inputs, not verified evidence.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (named counterparts per function)
- House baseline request-list template
- Repository from P0.6 and comms channel from P0.5

### Outputs / Evidence

- Issued request list with per-item owner and due date
- Request log showing the status of every item
- Received documents filed under `01-client-inputs` with provenance and dates

### Acceptance criteria

- At least 80 percent of items received, every outstanding item escalated to the sponsor
- Request log current and shared at the W1 call
- All received items filed with provenance noted
- Phase 1 fieldwork (P1.1-P1.6, P1.9) confirmed unblocked or blockers named

issues.name: Conduct ISO 27001 clauses 4-10 gap assessment
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Work clause-by-clause through ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clauses 4-10 using the house gap checklist, one row per requirement (4.1-4.4 context, 5.1-5.3 leadership, 6.1-6.3 planning, 7.1-7.5 support, 8.1-8.3 operation, 9.1-9.3 evaluation, 10.1-10.2 improvement). Rate each requirement **met**, **partial** or **missing** and write a one-line note naming the evidence seen or the gap.

Manoj leads; the method is document review of the P0.8 baseline pack plus short targeted interviews with the sponsor, ISMS owner and IT lead named in the P0.1 charter. Do not draft fixes here — findings only; remediation is planned in P1.10 and built in Phase 2.

Expect the management-system clauses to be largely `missing` at a factory whose partial implementation is technical: that is normal, Phase 2 exists to build them. Where something partial exists (for example an old policy written for a customer audit), capture it as reusable input for the Phase 2 drafting tasks.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.8 (baseline client inputs: org chart, existing policies, prior audits)
- Output of P0.1 (charter, named counterparts) and P0.2 (scope statement)
- House clause 4-10 gap checklist template
- Interview time with sponsor, ISMS owner and IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- Completed clause 4-10 gap sheet with per-requirement ratings and notes, filed in the evidence repository under the clause taxonomy (P0.6)
- List of reusable existing documents flagged for Phase 2 drafting
- Gap rows ready for merge into the combined report (P1.10)

### Acceptance criteria

- Every clause 4-10 requirement rated met, partial or missing
- Each rating carries a written note naming the evidence seen or the gap
- Gap sheet filed in the evidence repository and referenced by P1.10

issues.name: Interview process owners (IT, HR, production, procurement, facilities)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Interview the owners of the five in-scope functions: IT, HR, production, procurement and facilities. Masha schedules all sessions, sends a short agenda in advance and scribes; Manoj leads the IT sessions and joins others where technical depth is needed. Target 60-90 minutes per function.

The purpose is actual-versus-claimed practice, so ask open, concrete questions ("show me what happened when the last person left — what happened to their account?") rather than reading policy statements aloud. Where an answer conflicts with documents from P0.8, note the conflict without challenging the interviewee; it becomes a gap row, not a dispute.

Factory practicalities: book production supervisors around shift handovers rather than mid-shift, keep questions plain and jargon-free for shop-floor managers, and prefer walk-and-talk on the floor — it surfaces reality better than a meeting room. Write notes into the per-function template the same day while memory is fresh.

Findings feed the clause gap sheet (P1.1), the A.5 and A.6 assessments (P1.5, P1.6) and the Phase 2 risk workshops (P2.4).

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (named counterparts per function)
- Output of P0.5 (contact sheet and comms plan for scheduling)
- Output of P0.8 (documents to test claims against)
- House interview question set per function

### Outputs / Evidence

- Five per-function interview note files in the evidence repository (P0.6 taxonomy)
- Conflict list of claimed versus observed practice, tagged to controls
- Scheduling record with attendance

### Acceptance criteria

- All five functions interviewed
- Notes filed per function in the evidence repository
- Conflicts and follow-ups tagged for P1.1, P1.5, P1.6 and P2.4

issues.name: Verify existing technological controls hands-on (A.8 / ISA ch. 5)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

This is the core verify-before-document task. Manoj sits at the consoles with the client IT lead and verifies every claimed technological control first-hand: AD/IAM (user list against HR roster, privileged accounts, MFA state), firewall rulebase and remote access, endpoint protection coverage against the device list, backup jobs with last-success timestamps, logging reach and retention, patch levels on servers and clients, and encryption at rest. Accept nothing verbal — if it cannot be shown on screen it is `missing`.

Work through the dual-mapped tracker (P0.7) A.8 rows plus VDA ISA chapter 5 (and chapter 4 for IAM), marking each row **exists-verified**, **partial** or **missing**; verified-by is Manoj only. Capture screenshots and config exports as you go, hostname and system clock visible where possible, and hand them to Masha for same-day filing — loose evidence dies in laptops.

Sequence for a factory: server room systems and ERP first, then endpoints, then network. Note any OT or production-machinery network interfaces observed; they feed the asset inventory (P1.9) and later risk workshops.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.8 (IT asset list, network diagram)
- Output of P0.7 (dual-mapped control tracker)
- Console access accompanied by the client IT lead
- Output of P1.2 (IT interview notes — the claims to test)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Tracker A.8 and ISA chapter 4-5 rows rated and signed by Manoj
- Screenshots and config exports filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Technical findings list feeding P1.7 scoring and the P1.10 backlog

### Acceptance criteria

- No A.8 tracker row left unassessed
- Every assessed row signed by Manoj as verifier
- Evidence artifacts filed and linked in time for P1.8 consolidation

issues.name: Walk the site: physical & environmental controls (A.7 / ISA ch. 3)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Walk the entire site first as a visitor would experience it, then as an insider: perimeter and gates, reception and visitor handling, badge issuance and wearing, CCTV coverage and actual recorded retention, the server room (access control, access logging, cooling, fire suppression, water and dust risk — leather processing puts dust and chemicals nearby), secure storage areas, and clear-desk and clear-screen reality in the offices and the production office.

Manoj assesses against Annex A A.7 and VDA ISA chapter 3; Masha photographs and logs each observation with location and time. Obtain written client permission for photography first, and avoid capturing staff faces or customer-identifiable parts — automotive customers are sensitive about part imagery.

Test controls rather than viewing them: arrive at reception unannounced to try the visitor process, ask who holds server-room keys and who last entered, and ask to see CCTV playback from a specific past day to prove retention. Log every gap immediately; the list feeds the P3.8 physical remediation task directly.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (facilities counterpart available for the walk)
- Output of P0.7 (tracker A.7 and ISA chapter 3 rows)
- Site access for both consultants and photography permission
- Site plan or layout drawing from P0.8 where available

### Outputs / Evidence

- Walkthrough report with per-area findings, filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Time-stamped photo log tied to findings
- Tracker A.7 and ISA chapter 3 rows rated, gaps tagged for P3.8

### Acceptance criteria

- Walkthrough report completed covering all listed areas
- Photo evidence attached to each finding
- Gaps recorded in the tracker and referenced by the P1.10 backlog

issues.name: Assess organisational, supplier & compliance controls (A.5 / ISA ch. 1)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj assesses the organisational control set — Annex A A.5 and VDA ISA chapter 1 — against what actually operates, not what paper claims: policies in live use (who has read them, when last approved), asset and information records practice, classification and labelling behaviour, supplier management, and the legal and regulatory register.

For suppliers, sample contracts from the P0.8 supplier list by criticality rather than volume — IT vendors, logistics and chemical suppliers first — checking for security clauses, NDAs and audit rights. For the legal register, cover UAE PDPL (Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021), the automotive customer's TISAX requirement from P0.3, labour-law record duties, and any free-zone or municipality rules for the site. A UAE leather factory rarely holds such a register; expect to record it `missing` and seed its structure for Phase 2.

Use the P1.2 procurement and management interview notes as the claims to test. Every A.5 tracker row gets an evidence link or an explicit gap note — partial credit requires an artifact.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.8 (existing policies, supplier list, contracts)
- Output of P1.2 (procurement and management interview notes)
- Output of P0.7 (tracker A.5 and ISA chapter 1 rows)
- Output of P0.3 (TISAX objective memo)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Tracker A.5 and ISA chapter 1 rows completed with evidence links or gap notes
- Supplier contract sampling notes in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Legal register skeleton handed to Phase 2 drafting

### Acceptance criteria

- All A.5 rows completed with evidence or an explicit gap note
- Supplier sample reviewed and documented
- Legal register status recorded and its gap fed to P1.10

issues.name: Assess people/HR controls and records (A.6 / ISA ch. 2)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha assesses people controls — Annex A A.6 and VDA ISA chapter 2 — by sampling at least 10 staff files across the workforce mix: office staff, IT, production operators and outsourced or contract labour (common in UAE factories). For each file check pre-employment screening (references, qualification and visa checks where lawful), a signed NDA or confidentiality clause, security responsibilities in the employment contract, onboarding and offboarding records, and evidence of disciplinary process awareness.

Handle personnel records with care: review on-site with HR present, record findings in an anonymised sampling sheet using file reference codes rather than names, and do not copy personnel documents into the evidence repository — PDPL applies. The sampling sheet itself is the evidence artifact.

Building on the P1.2 HR interview, walk the joiner-mover-leaver process end to end and ask one pointed question: who tells IT when someone leaves, and how fast? That answer usually exposes the largest A.6 gap. Manoj reviews and signs the findings before they enter the tracker.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.8 (HR roster to draw the sample from)
- Output of P1.2 (HR interview notes)
- HR counterpart available and on-site access to files
- Output of P0.7 (tracker A.6 and ISA chapter 2 rows)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Anonymised sampling sheet covering at least 10 files, filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Tracker A.6 and ISA chapter 2 rows rated with findings
- Gap notes feeding P1.10 and remediation task P3.10

### Acceptance criteria

- Sample of at least 10 staff files reviewed across staff categories
- Findings recorded without copying personnel documents into the repository
- Findings signed off by Manoj in the tracker

issues.name: Score initial VDA ISA 6.0 self-assessment (all IS requirements)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj scores the initial TISAX self-assessment in the official VDA ISA 6.0 Excel (Information Security module) obtained via the ENX participant account. Score every requirement — including the should requirements and the additional requirements for high protection needs, which apply per the P0.3 scoping memo — with a maturity level 0-5, strictly from the findings verified in P1.3 through P1.6. No aspirational scoring: an AL2 assessor tests plausibility against evidence, and an inflated baseline destroys the value of the P3.16 re-score delta.

Apply the ISA maturity logic honestly: a control that exists and works but has no documented process caps at ML2; ML3 requires defined, documented and demonstrably practised. Expect a first-pass overall result well below 3 — that is the point, it sizes the Phase 2 and Phase 3 workload.

Record a one-line justification per requirement referencing the evidence or gap note, then cross-check every score against the dual-mapped tracker (P0.7) so the ISO and TISAX views never diverge. Resolve discrepancies now, not in Phase 3.

### Inputs

- Official VDA ISA 6.0 Excel via the ENX portal account (P0.4)
- Output of P0.3 (AL2, IS module, high protection, ML3 memo)
- Outputs of P1.3, P1.4, P1.5 and P1.6 (verified findings)
- Output of P0.7 (dual-mapped tracker)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Scored VDA ISA 6.0 file v1.0 filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Per-requirement justification notes
- Sub-ML3 requirement list feeding P1.10

### Acceptance criteria

- No IS-module requirement left unscored, high-protection extras included
- Every score cross-checked against the tracker with discrepancies resolved
- Baseline scoring file versioned and filed for comparison at P3.16

issues.name: Compile evidence register of verified existing controls
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha consolidates all evidence captured during verification fieldwork — P1.3 technical artifacts, the P1.4 walkthrough photo log, P1.5 organisational evidence and the P1.6 anonymised sampling sheet — into a single evidence register. One row per artifact: artifact name and repository path, control mapping (Annex A reference plus ISA requirement), capture date, verifier (Manoj) and status.

Work incrementally: file artifacts the same day fieldwork produces them rather than batching at the end — the due date only holds if the register grows daily from early August. Chase Manoj immediately for unlabelled screenshots; an unattributed screenshot is worthless three weeks later.

Then reconcile against the dual-mapped tracker (P0.7): every row marked verified-exists must resolve to a working evidence link, and every register artifact must map to at least one tracker row. Correct file names to the P0.6 conventions as you file. This register becomes the backbone of the P3.15 evidence packs and the P5.7 handover pack, so structural debt introduced here compounds for the rest of the engagement.

### Inputs

- Outputs of P1.3, P1.4 and P1.5 (evidence artifacts) and P1.6 (sampling sheet)
- Output of P0.6 (repository taxonomy and naming conventions)
- Output of P0.7 (tracker rows to reconcile against)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Evidence register v1.0 filed in the evidence repository
- Repository artifacts renamed and filed per convention
- Reconciliation note listing tracker rows still lacking evidence

### Acceptance criteria

- Every tracker row marked verified-exists has a working evidence link
- Register rows carry artifact, control mapping, capture date and verifier
- Reconciliation gaps reported to Manoj before P1.10 drafting

issues.name: Compile information asset inventory with owners and classification
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha builds the information asset inventory from the P0.8 baseline lists plus everything surfaced during interviews and fieldwork. Cover all asset types, not just IT hardware: servers, endpoints, network devices, the ERP and production planning systems, file shares and key datasets — customer part specifications and drawings from automotive customers are the crown jewels for TISAX — plus paper records and production machinery with network-connected controllers noted during P1.3 and P1.4.

Assign each asset a named owner, a role plus the current person, confirmed with that person rather than assumed. Classify per the client's handling rules if any exist; otherwise apply an interim four-level scheme (public, internal, confidential, secret) aligned with what the P2.13 classification policy will formalise, and mark it interim.

Prioritise completeness on critical assets over exhaustiveness on trivia: the register must be workshop-ready for the P2.4 risk assessment, where asset-owner pairs anchor the discussion. Reference ISO 27001 A.5.9 to A.5.12 and the VDA ISA chapter 1 asset requirements so the register doubles as control evidence in the tracker.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.8 (IT asset lists, org chart, network diagram)
- Outputs of P1.2 (interviews) and P1.3/P1.4 (assets observed in fieldwork)
- Client asset owners available to confirm ownership
- Output of P0.6 (repository filing conventions)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Asset inventory v1.0 with owner and classification columns, filed in the evidence repository
- Interim classification scheme note for P2.13
- Critical-asset shortlist prepared for the P2.4 risk workshops

### Acceptance criteria

- All critical assets listed with confirmed named owners
- Every listed asset classified, with interim scheme flagged where used
- Register accepted as input to the P2.4 workshop preparation

issues.name: Produce combined gap report and prioritised remediation backlog
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj merges the three gap streams into one combined report: clause 4-10 gaps (P1.1), Annex A control gaps from the verification tasks (P1.3 to P1.6 via the tracker), and every VDA ISA requirement scoring below ML3 (P1.7). Deduplicate through the dual-mapped tracker so a single remediation item closes both frameworks — this dedup is what makes two frameworks fit in a single delivery window.

Rate each gap for severity (certification or assessment blocker, major, minor) and effort (quick fix, project, purchase-dependent). Convert the rated list into a prioritised remediation backlog where every item names its owning Phase 3 task (P3.1 to P3.14 by theme) or Phase 2 documentation task. Purchase-dependent items are explicitly flagged for P3.0 so procurement requests are raised immediately — purchase orders must land by 2026-09-11 to protect the Phase 3 tail.

Write the report for the sponsor, not for auditors: a two-page summary with counts, top risks and the decision being asked for at P1.11, followed by the full gap table. Masha proofreads and files; Manoj owns the content.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.1 (clause gap sheet)
- Outputs of P1.3 to P1.6 via the tracker (P0.7) and the P1.8 evidence register
- Output of P1.7 (sub-ML3 requirement list)
- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory for impact context)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Combined gap report v1.0 filed in the evidence repository
- Prioritised remediation backlog with task references
- Purchase-dependent item list handed to P3.0

### Acceptance criteria

- Every gap row references a remediation or documentation task
- Severity and effort rated on all rows
- Purchase-dependent items flagged and dated for P3.0

issues.name: Present gap findings; management sign-off on remediation plan
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

The formal Phase 1 gate and the project's declared re-baseline point. Manoj presents the combined gap report and remediation backlog (P1.10) to the sponsor and management team; Masha organises the session, takes minutes and captures decisions verbatim. Hold it on-site and in person — this is where the client commits money and people.

Walk management through what verification found versus what was claimed, the prioritised backlog, what each business function owns, and the procurement list with the 08-18 purchase-order deadline and its consequence for the Phase 3 schedule. Ask explicitly for three commitments: the priority order approved, a named client owner per backlog theme, and procurement sign-off. If gap volume exceeds the plan's assumptions, re-baseline here — adjust scope, dates or resourcing openly rather than absorbing silently; this option expires with this meeting.

Minutes are signed by the sponsor the same day and confirmed at the Week 3 status call. The signed minutes are themselves ISO clause 5.1 leadership evidence — file them accordingly in the evidence repository.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.10 (gap report and prioritised backlog)
- Sponsor and management availability booked via the P0.5 comms plan
- Procurement counterpart present to commit to the purchase list
- Output of P0.1 (charter escalation terms, in case re-baseline is needed)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed meeting minutes filed in the evidence repository
- Approved remediation backlog v1.0 and procurement commitment list
- Re-baseline note, or explicit confirmation that none is needed

### Acceptance criteria

- Minutes signed by the sponsor approving the backlog and procurement list
- Named client owner recorded per backlog theme
- Re-baseline decision explicitly documented either way

issues.name: Draft context, interested parties, ISMS manual & roles/RACI (cl 4, 5.3)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts the clause 4 pack. Context of the organisation (clause 4.1): internal and external issues — automotive supply-chain security demands, UAE regulatory environment, single-site factory operations, dependence on ERP and a small IT team. Interested parties (clause 4.2): automotive customers (the TISAX expectation, citing the customer request attached in P0.3), ENX, the certification body, employees, suppliers and UAE authorities, each with their requirements stated.

Keep the ISMS manual thin: an umbrella document that points to the scope (P0.2), the policy (P2.2), the risk method (P2.3) and the process landscape rather than duplicating them. For clause 5.3, extend the P0.1 project RACI into an operating ISMS RACI: ISMS owner, risk owners, control owners and incident manager, with deputies — and name the production manager's security responsibilities explicitly.

Manoj reviews for accuracy against Phase 1 interview findings; formal approval happens at P2.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.1 (RACI, named counterparts)
- Output of P0.2 (ISMS scope statement v1.0)
- Org chart and baseline inputs from P0.8
- Interview notes from P1.2
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Context analysis and interested-parties register filed under the clause-4 folder
- ISMS manual v0.9 referencing scope, policy and risk method
- Operating ISMS RACI filed under clause-5

### Acceptance criteria

- Context covers internal and external issues relevant to the scope
- Every interested party has documented requirements, including the automotive customer's TISAX expectation
- ISMS RACI names owner, risk owners, control owners and incident manager
- Manoj review completed; documents queued for P2.15 approval

issues.name: Draft Information Security Policy + measurable objectives (cl 5.2, 6.2)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts the top-level Information Security Policy against clause 5.2: appropriate to Al Kazhnah's purpose, committing to satisfy applicable requirements and to continual improvement, and providing the framework for objectives. Keep it to two pages management will actually sign, and note VDA ISA 1.1.1 expects the same policy — cover protection of automotive-customer information explicitly.

Draft the clause 6.2 objectives as a separate register, each entry measurable with metric, target, owner, method and reporting date. Anchor them in engagement reality: all staff trained by the P4.2 sessions, a successful restore test (P3.5), incident response exercised (P3.12), target maturity level 3 across VDA ISA chapters at the P3.16 re-score, and patch SLA compliance. Objectives are reported into the management review (P4.8, P4.9), so pick metrics the client can keep measuring after handover.

Manoj reviews target plausibility; sponsor sign-off happens at P2.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.3 (confirmed TISAX objective, target ML3)
- Output of P1.10 (gap report, to set realistic targets)
- Draft context and interested parties from P2.1
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Information Security Policy v0.9 filed under clause-5
- Objectives register with metrics and owners filed under clause-6

### Acceptance criteria

- Policy satisfies every clause 5.2 requirement and names automotive-customer information
- Each objective has metric, target value, owner and measurement date
- Objectives include the TISAX ML3 target
- Manoj review complete; both documents queued for P2.15 sign-off

issues.name: Write risk assessment methodology (cl 6.1, ISO 27005-aligned, ISA 1.4)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj writes the methodology so risk results are reproducible (clause 6.1.2) and defensible at both audits. Align with ISO 27005: asset- and scenario-based identification, a 5x5 likelihood and impact matrix, and impact anchors written for this factory — hours of production downtime, leakage of automotive-customer drawings and specifications, contract loss, and safety or regulatory consequences in the UAE.

Define risk acceptance criteria and appetite explicitly and have the sponsor endorse them before any workshop scores a risk — retrofitting appetite after scoring invalidates decisions. Specify roles (every risk gets a named client risk owner), the four treatment options, the annual review cycle, and re-assessment triggers such as major change or incident. Cover VDA ISA 1.4.1 expectations in the same document so one method serves both frameworks.

Keep the method simple enough for the client to rerun without consultants — that is what maturity level 3 requires. Masha formats, files, and prepares the scoring sheets used in P2.4.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.1 (context and interested parties, draft acceptable)
- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory with owners)
- Output of P1.10 (gap report)
- House ISO 27005-aligned methodology template

### Outputs / Evidence

- Risk assessment methodology v1.0 filed under clause-6
- Scoring matrix and workshop scoring sheets ready for P2.4

### Acceptance criteria

- Scales, impact anchors and acceptance criteria defined and reproducible
- Sponsor endorses the risk appetite in writing before workshops start
- VDA ISA 1.4 requirements addressed in the same method
- Scoring sheets issued unchanged to P2.4

issues.name: Run risk assessment workshops with asset/process owners
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Run three to five workshops grouped by process area — IT, production and OT, HR and administration, procurement and supply chain, facilities — with the owners named in P0.1. Manoj facilitates identification and scoring strictly per the P2.3 method; Masha schedules around factory shifts, scribes into the scoring sheets, and keeps attendance records.

Work through the P1.9 asset inventory group by group and use verified Phase 1 findings (P1.3-P1.6) as the vulnerability evidence, not opinions. Push on factory-specific scenarios: ERP outage halting dispatch, production machinery and PLCs on a flat network, confidentiality of customer CAD data and specifications (the TISAX driver), single-site dependency, and UAE summer power or cooling failure in the server room.

Time-box scoring and park disputes for Manoj's post-workshop moderation rather than letting one risk consume a session. Capture a candidate risk owner for every entry before each workshop closes.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.3 (methodology v1.0 and scoring sheets)
- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory)
- Verified findings from P1.3, P1.4, P1.5 and P1.6
- Output of P1.10 (gap report)
- Owner availability confirmed via P0.5 channels

### Outputs / Evidence

- Completed scoring sheets per workshop, filed under clause-6
- Attendance records for every session
- Consolidated raw risk list handed to P2.5

### Acceptance criteria

- All P1.9 asset groups covered by at least one workshop
- Every session has an attendance record filed
- Every raw risk names asset, threat, vulnerability and candidate owner
- Raw list delivered to P2.5 by 14 August

issues.name: Populate risk register with scored risks and treatment decisions
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj consolidates the raw workshop output into the risk register: de-duplicate, normalise wording, and moderate scores across workshops so a 4 means the same in IT as in production. Score strictly per P2.3 and record the calculation, not just the result.

Assign every risk a named client risk owner — never a consultant — and record the clause 6.1.3 treatment decision: modify, retain, avoid or share. Any retained risk above the appetite line needs documented management acceptance signed by the risk owner and sponsor; collect these signatures now rather than on audit eve. Cross-link each modify decision to the Annex A controls and VDA ISA requirements in the P0.7 tracker so treatment traceability stays mechanical.

Masha checks completeness against the P1.9 asset groups and files the register. Treat it as a living document: it is re-reviewed at the management review (P4.9) and after the P3.16 re-score.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.4 (scoring sheets and raw risk list)
- Output of P2.3 (methodology and appetite)
- P0.7 control tracker for cross-linking
- Output of P1.10 (gap report)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Risk register v1.0 with scores, owners and treatment decisions, filed under clause-6
- Signed acceptance records for retained risks above appetite

### Acceptance criteria

- Every workshop risk appears once, scored per the methodology
- Every risk has a named client owner and a treatment decision
- Retained risks above appetite carry signed acceptances
- Register rows cross-linked to the P0.7 tracker

issues.name: Draft risk treatment plan linked to remediation backlog
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj turns the register's modify decisions into the clause 6.1.3 risk treatment plan: for each risk, the selected controls mapped to Annex A and VDA ISA, concrete actions, a named owner, deadline, resource needs, and the expected residual risk after treatment.

Do not invent a parallel workstream — link each plan entry to the P1.10 remediation backlog and to its Phase 3 board task (P3.0-P3.14), and reference the plan line in those tasks, so plan and board remain one thing and progress reporting is a filter, not a reconciliation exercise. Route any hardware or licence purchase into P3.0 immediately; UAE procurement lead times will not compress later.

Get each risk owner's written agreement to their actions and dates, and give the sponsor visibility of the aggregate residual risk. The set of necessary controls from this plan is a direct input to the SoA (P2.7). Masha files the plan and keeps cross-references current.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.5 (risk register v1.0)
- Output of P1.10 (prioritised remediation backlog)
- P0.7 control tracker
- Phase 3 task list from the project board

### Outputs / Evidence

- Risk treatment plan v1.0 filed under clause-6
- Cross-reference table linking each plan line to a P3 task ID
- Risk owner agreements recorded

### Acceptance criteria

- Every modify risk has actions, owner, deadline and residual risk
- Every plan line maps to a P3 task ID and back
- Procurement-dependent actions raised via P3.0
- Risk owners have agreed their actions in writing

issues.name: Draft Statement of Applicability (93 Annex A controls)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj derives the Statement of Applicability from the P0.7 tracker rather than starting a fresh document: all 93 Annex A controls, applicability with justification, and implementation status. Justifications must be specific — tie each applicable control to risks in the P2.5 register, the P2.6 treatment plan, legal obligations, or the automotive customer's contractual requirements; boilerplate justification is the first thing a certification auditor flags.

Expect few or no exclusions at a manufacturer with IT, OT, HR, suppliers and a physical site; where a control is excluded, write the justification so it survives challenge. Status must reflect the verified state from Phase 1 fieldwork (P1.3-P1.6), not the client's claimed state — partial is an honest, acceptable answer now, because the SoA is re-issued at P3.16 after remediation.

Masha formats and files; Manoj signs and dates. Version it properly: the Stage 1 auditor and the TISAX assessor will both ask for the current SoA by version.

### Inputs

- P0.7 tracker with the verified-by column populated
- Output of P2.5 (risk register) and P2.6 (treatment plan)
- Verification results from P1.3-P1.6
- Customer contractual security requirements gathered in P0.3

### Outputs / Evidence

- SoA v1.0, signed and dated, filed under clause-6
- Tracker updated with completed SoA columns

### Acceptance criteria

- All 93 controls listed with applicability and specific justification
- Status matches verified evidence, not claims
- Exclusions, if any, individually justified
- Signed by Manoj; re-issue at P3.16 scheduled

issues.name: Draft access control, IAM & authentication policies
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts three linked documents: an access control policy (A.5.15, A.5.18), an identity management procedure covering the joiner-mover-leaver process (A.5.16, A.6.5), and an authentication standard (A.5.17, A.8.5), matching VDA ISA chapter 4. Trigger JML from HR events so departures lose access the same day — connect the procedure to the HR records assessed in P1.6.

Write for the real environment verified in P1.3: role-based access per function; explicit handling of shared shop-floor terminals and generic accounts — TISAX assessors probe shared logins hard, so document the compensating controls or the removal plan; privileged access separation with named admin accounts (A.8.2); MFA scope for remote and administrative access; a password standard; and a quarterly access review with a named review owner.

State the target enforceable state that P3.1 will implement and Manoj will verify — a policy the factory cannot follow becomes an audit finding. Manoj reviews feasibility before the drafts are queued for P2.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified IAM state) and P1.6 (HR records)
- Output of P1.10 (IAM gaps)
- Interview notes from P1.2
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Access control policy, IAM procedure and authentication standard v0.9 filed under the A.5/A.8 and ISA chapter-4 folders

### Acceptance criteria

- JML, privileged access, MFA, password rules and quarterly reviews all covered
- Shared and generic account handling explicitly addressed
- Consistent with the P3.1 remediation plan
- Manoj feasibility review complete; queued for P2.15

issues.name: Draft ops & crypto procedures (backup, logging, malware, patch, change, keys)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts six short operational procedures mapped to Annex A and VDA ISA chapter 5: backup and restore (A.8.13), logging and monitoring (A.8.15, A.8.16), malware protection (A.8.7), vulnerability and patch management (A.8.8), change management (A.8.32), and cryptography with key management (A.8.24). One procedure per topic, two to four pages, naming the tools actually deployed as verified in P1.3 — never document a tool the client does not run; name the planned Phase 3 replacement instead.

Make each procedure operable by the client IT lead: schedules, responsibilities, and the records produced. Backup must state scope (ERP, file server, domain controllers), retention, an offline or immutable copy, and the test cadence that P3.5 will prove. Patch windows must respect production shifts so reboots never stop a line unplanned. Keep cryptography pragmatic: disk encryption, TLS, key custody and recovery.

Manoj reviews each procedure for technical correctness — these documents are the yardstick his Phase 3 verifications (P3.2-P3.7) measure against.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified tooling and configurations)
- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory) and P1.10 (gaps)
- Draft P2.8 documents for consistency
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Six procedures v0.9 filed under the A.8 and ISA chapter-5 folders

### Acceptance criteria

- All six topics drafted with schedules, owners and records defined
- Content matches deployed tooling or names the planned Phase 3 change
- Backup procedure aligns with the P3.5 restore test design
- Manoj technical review complete; queued for P2.15

issues.name: Draft incident response & crisis management procedure
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts the incident response and crisis management procedure against A.5.24-A.5.28 and VDA ISA chapter 1.6. Start with a severity matrix and clear definitions, then the lifecycle: detection and reporting, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, evidence preservation (A.5.28), and post-incident review feeding lessons back into the ISMS.

Reporting channels must work for the whole factory: a phone number and supervisor route for shop-floor workers without email, cover for night shifts, and a single incident manager role staffed from the P2.1 RACI with a deputy. Include the notification step TISAX expects — automotive customers are informed when an incident affects their information, using the contact from the P0.5 stakeholder register — and add UAE regulatory notification where applicable. Define the escalation threshold into crisis mode and the interface to the BC/DR plan (P2.11).

Build the contact tree and an incident log template into the document. Write it to be exercised: the P3.12 tabletop runs this procedure as written, and gaps found there are cheaper than gaps found in a real incident.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.1 (operating RACI, incident manager named)
- Output of P0.5 (stakeholder and customer contacts)
- Findings from P1.2 and P1.3
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Incident response and crisis procedure v0.9 with severity matrix and contact tree
- Incident log template filed with the procedure

### Acceptance criteria

- Reporting route exists for shop-floor and night-shift staff
- Customer notification step documented
- Crisis escalation and the P2.11 interface defined
- Log template created; procedure booked for the P3.12 exercise; queued for P2.15

issues.name: Draft BC/DR plan with BIA for production-critical systems
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj runs a business impact analysis before writing any plan: with production, IT and finance owners, list the critical processes — order intake, production scheduling, ERP, dispatch, payroll — and set MTPD, RTO and RPO per supporting system, recording dependencies such as the single server room, power and cooling, and connectivity. UAE factory reality: summer grid or cooling failure is a top scenario; treat it as a design case, not a footnote.

Then draft the BC/DR plan per A.5.29 and A.5.30: activation criteria and authority, a recovery team with deputies, per-system recovery procedures in priority order, workarounds that keep production moving on paper while IT recovers, and communications. RPOs must match what the P2.9 backup procedure actually delivers and what the P3.5 restore test will prove — a 4-hour RPO on nightly backups is fiction. Interface cleanly with the crisis escalation in P2.10.

Masha documents and files; Manoj owns the technical recovery content. The plan is exercised at P3.13, so keep every step concrete enough to walk through.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory) plus P1.3 and P1.4 findings
- Draft backup procedure from P2.9
- Draft incident and crisis procedure from P2.10
- Process owner availability for BIA sessions

### Outputs / Evidence

- BIA record with MTPD, RTO and RPO per critical system
- BC/DR plan v0.9 filed under the A.5 and ISA chapter-1 folders

### Acceptance criteria

- BIA covers all production-critical systems with agreed RTO and RPO
- Recovery steps documented per critical system in priority order
- RPOs consistent with P2.9 backups and the P3.5 restore test
- Crisis interface to P2.10 defined; queued for P2.15 and the P3.13 exercise

issues.name: Draft supplier security policy + supplier register with contract clauses
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts the supplier security policy against A.5.19-A.5.22 and VDA ISA chapter 6, then builds the supplier register from the P0.8 supplier list and the P1.5 assessment. Tier suppliers by what they can touch: IT and ERP providers with system access, logistics carriers handling customer shipment data, and on-site services — cleaning, maintenance, security guards — with physical access to production. Effort follows tier; a chemicals vendor with no data access needs a register line, not an assessment.

Draft a standard security clause annex that procurement can attach to purchase orders and contracts: confidentiality, incident notification within a defined time, right to audit, data return or destruction at exit, and subcontracting approval. Protection of automotive-customer information passed downstream is the TISAX assessor's core interest here — call it out explicitly.

This task carries the Client-Action label because procurement owns issuing the clauses: agree the rollout owner and sequence now, since execution and key-supplier assessments happen in P3.11.

### Inputs

- Supplier list and contracts from P0.8
- Output of P1.5 (supplier and compliance control assessment)
- Procurement counterpart named in P0.1
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Supplier security policy v0.9 and tiered supplier register
- Contract security clause annex, filed under the A.5 and ISA chapter-6 folders

### Acceptance criteria

- Register lists suppliers with tier and access type
- Clause annex approved by procurement for use
- Policy covers onboarding, monitoring and exit
- P3.11 rollout owner and sequence agreed; queued for P2.15

issues.name: Draft HR, acceptable use, classification, physical & telework policy bundle
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha drafts five short policies as one bundle with shared terminology. HR security (A.6.1-A.6.6): screening within UAE labour-law norms, security terms in contracts, the disciplinary process, and termination steps with same-day asset return and access revocation, wired to the P2.8 leaver process. Acceptable use (A.5.10): one plain-language page for a multilingual workforce, with a translated summary planned for shop-floor noticeboards. Information classification (A.5.12, A.5.13): a simple three-level scheme with handling rules per level, placing automotive-customer CAD files and specifications in the top tier. Physical security (A.7, ISA chapter 3): zones exactly as observed in the P1.4 walk — perimeter, production floor, server room — plus visitor registration and contractor escort rules. Telework and mobile devices (A.6.7, A.8.1): remote work for office staff and the device stance that P3.14 will implement.

Use one classification vocabulary across every document — inconsistent labels are a favourite audit finding. Manoj reviews the bundle; the P4.1 awareness materials are built directly from these policies, so clarity now saves rework later.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.4 (site walk findings) and P1.6 (HR assessment)
- Interview notes from P1.2
- Draft P2.8 documents for JML consistency
- Document conventions from P2.14

### Outputs / Evidence

- Five policies v0.9 filed under their A.5, A.6, A.7 and ISA chapter folders

### Acceptance criteria

- All five topics drafted with consistent classification vocabulary
- Classification scheme has handling rules per level
- Physical policy reflects the zones observed in P1.4
- Manoj review complete; queued for P2.15

issues.name: Establish document control procedure + master document register (cl 7.5)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Do this first in the Phase 2 wave — it is due 13 August precisely so every policy drafted in P2.8-P2.13 is born controlled rather than retrofitted. Masha formalises the P0.6 repository conventions into a clause 7.5 document control procedure: document identification, format, a review-and-approval authority matrix (who approves policies versus procedures), version numbering, publication and distribution, control of documents of external origin, retention, and withdrawal of obsolete versions.

Build the master document register alongside: every existing and planned ISMS document with ID, title, owner, version, status, approval date and next review date. Seed it immediately with the full Phase 2 document list so progress toward P2.15 is visible at a glance.

Issue a document template with a standard header block — ID, version, owner, approval — and hand it to Manoj and every author before drafting starts. Masha maintains the register through to the completeness check (P5.6) and the handover pack (P5.7).

### Inputs

- Output of P0.6 (repository and naming readme)
- House document-control template
- List of all planned Phase 2 documents

### Outputs / Evidence

- Document control procedure v1.0 filed under clause-7
- Master document register live at the repository root
- Document template with header block distributed to authors

### Acceptance criteria

- Procedure addresses every clause 7.5.2 and 7.5.3 requirement
- Register lists all existing and planned ISMS documents with owners
- Template adopted by all Phase 2 authors
- Procedure in force before the P2.8-P2.13 drafting wave completes

issues.name: Hold policy approval workshop; management sign-off + publication
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

This is the gate that turns drafts into an operating ISMS. Masha pre-circulates the full Phase 2 set at v0.9 — the P2.1-P2.3 documents, the risk register and treatment plan (P2.5, P2.6), the SoA (P2.7) and the policy bundle (P2.8-P2.13) — at least three days ahead with a one-page summary per document, and logs every comment with its resolution.

Manoj runs the half-day workshop with the sponsor and management team, walking the set by theme and forcing the real decisions into the open: risk acceptance criteria, retained residual risks, SoA justifications, and what the policies oblige staff to do. Capture minuted, signed approval per document; a document with open issues gets a dated follow-up action, never a silent deferral.

Then publish: raise approved documents to v1.0, update the P2.14 register, and communicate through the P0.5 channels — email for office staff, supervisors and translated noticeboard summaries for the shop floor. File the communication evidence; both auditors will ask how a machine operator knows the rules. Publication evidence feeds straight into the P4.1 and P4.2 awareness work.

### Inputs

- All Phase 2 documents at v0.9 with reviews complete
- Master document register from P2.14
- Sponsor and management team availability
- Communication channels defined in P0.5

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed approval minutes covering every document
- Register updated to v1.0 approved status
- Publication and communication evidence filed

### Acceptance criteria

- Every Phase 2 document approved and signed, or carrying a dated follow-up
- Register shows v1.0 approved for all signed documents
- Publication evidence exists for office and shop-floor channels
- Comment log closed with resolutions recorded

issues.name: Raise procurement requests for remediation hardware/licences
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

The moment P1.11 sign-off lands, Masha converts every purchase-dependent item on the P1.10 backlog into a formal procurement request: specification, quantity, indicative budget and the Phase 3 task it unblocks. Manoj supplies the technical specs (typical items: EDR seats, firewall or Wi-Fi licences, MDM licences, backup storage, server-room lock and CCTV components, UPS). Do not batch and wait — issue requests the same day the backlog is approved.

Walk each request through the client procurement counterpart named in the P0.1 RACI. UAE reality: quotes, LPO approval and supplier lead times routinely eat two weeks, so purchase orders for Phase 3 blockers must land by **2026-09-11** to protect the Phase 3 tail.

Masha maintains a live procurement tracker — item, request date, quote status, PO number, expected delivery, blocked task — and tables it at every weekly call from W6 (Sep 4) onward. Anything slipping past its need-by date is escalated to the sponsor via the P0.5 escalation path, with a fallback compensating control agreed with Manoj.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.10 (purchase-dependent item list from the remediation backlog)
- Output of P1.11 (management sign-off and budget commitment)
- Named procurement counterpart from the P0.1 RACI
- Output of P0.5 (contact sheet and escalation path)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Submitted procurement request forms filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Live procurement tracker linked from the Phase 3 board
- Escalation notes for any at-risk item

### Acceptance criteria

- Every purchase-dependent backlog item has a submitted request with spec and need-by date
- Tracker live and reviewed at weekly calls from W6
- POs for Phase 3 blockers placed by 2026-09-11 or escalated with agreed fallback

issues.name: Remediate & verify IAM controls (JML, privileged access, MFA, reviews)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Work from the P1.3 verified state, not from claims. Manoj sits with the client IT lead and closes each IAM gap in sequence: reconcile AD against the HR roster and disable ghost or leaver accounts; split privileged access into named admin accounts (no shared domain admin); enforce MFA on remote access, admin logons and cloud consoles; then stand up the joiner-mover-leaver process with an HR trigger so P3.10 checklists drive account actions. This implements the P2.8 policy — ISO A.5.15-A.5.18, A.8.2, A.8.5 and VDA ISA chapter 4.

Factory specifics: shared shop-floor terminals are the usual finding. Replace generic logons with locked-down kiosk accounts where individual accounts are impractical, and document that as a risk-accepted exception.

Maturity level 3 needs operating evidence, not configuration alone: execute the first user access review and first privileged access review inside this task, signed by the reviewing manager. Manoj verifies every change on screen and signs the tracker rows; Masha files exports same-day for P3.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified IAM state and findings)
- Output of P1.10 (IAM items on the remediation backlog)
- Output of P2.8 (approved access control and authentication policies)
- Console access with the IT lead; HR roster

### Outputs / Evidence

- Before/after configuration evidence and account reconciliation in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- First access review and privileged access review records
- Tracker (P0.7) A.5.15-A.5.18 and ISA chapter 4 rows updated to **exists-verified**

### Acceptance criteria

- No unexplained or shared privileged accounts remain; exceptions risk-accepted in writing
- MFA demonstrated live on remote and admin access
- JML procedure operational with first completed records
- All in-scope tracker rows signed off by Manoj

issues.name: Remediate & verify endpoint & malware protection
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj drives endpoint coverage to 100% of the P1.9 inventory: every server, laptop and shop-floor PC either runs the managed EDR/AV agent reporting to a central console, or is a documented exception with compensating control. If new EDR seats were procured via P3.0, deploy them first; otherwise verify and tighten what exists — ISO A.8.1, A.8.7 and VDA ISA chapter 5.

The predictable factory finding is legacy machines wired to production machinery that cannot take an agent or a patch. Do not force-fit software onto them; isolate them on the OT segment (coordinate with P3.3), restrict USB and remote paths, and record the residual risk in the risk register (P2.5).

Verify, do not trust the dashboard: pull the console coverage report and diff it against the inventory, confirm signature/engine currency, and run an EICAR detection test on a sampled workstation and server as live proof. Enable USB device control in line with the media rules being operationalised in P3.9. Masha files console exports and test evidence same-day; Manoj signs.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory) and P1.3 (verified endpoint findings)
- Output of P3.0 (EDR/AV licences if procurement was required)
- Output of P2.9 (malware protection procedure)
- Access to the endpoint management console with the IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- Console coverage report reconciled against the inventory, filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- EICAR detection test evidence and USB-control configuration export
- Documented exception list with compensating controls; tracker (P0.7) rows updated

### Acceptance criteria

- Coverage report matches the asset inventory with zero unexplained gaps
- Exceptions documented, compensated and risk-accepted
- Detection test evidence filed and signed off by Manoj

issues.name: Remediate & verify network security (segmentation, firewall, Wi-Fi, VPN)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj remediates network security in a deliberate order: segmentation design first, then firewall rulebase, then Wi-Fi, then remote access. Separate the OT/production machinery network from the IT LAN, isolate guest Wi-Fi from everything corporate, and move corporate Wi-Fi to certificate or WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise authentication. Clean the firewall rulebase to deny-by-default: remove any-any rules, tie each rule to an owner and justification, and formally review the result. Remote access becomes VPN with MFA (the MFA itself lands in P3.1). References: ISO A.8.20-A.8.22, VDA ISA chapter 5.

Machinery vendors with standing remote-maintenance access are a classic automotive-supplier exposure: convert them to time-bounded, logged access, and flag those vendors to Masha for the P3.11 supplier assessments.

Change discipline matters in a factory — schedule firewall and switch changes outside production shifts, with the IT lead executing and rollback agreed in advance. Verification is by test, not diagram: run inter-segment reachability tests (blocked and allowed paths), confirm guest-to-corporate isolation, and export the reviewed rulebase. Masha files the evidence; Manoj signs.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified network findings) and P0.8 (network diagram)
- Output of P1.10 (network items on the remediation backlog)
- Output of P3.0 (firewall/Wi-Fi licences or hardware if procured)
- Agreed change window with the client IT lead and production manager

### Outputs / Evidence

- As-built segmentation diagram and reviewed firewall rulebase export in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Inter-segment reachability and guest-isolation test records
- Tracker (P0.7) rows updated to **exists-verified**

### Acceptance criteria

- As-built diagram matches the implemented segmentation
- Reachability tests evidence OT, guest and corporate isolation
- Rulebase reviewed, justified and signed off by Manoj
- Vendor remote-maintenance access time-bounded and logged

issues.name: Remediate & verify logging & monitoring
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj establishes centralised logging sized to the client, not to a SOC fantasy: a syslog collector or SIEM-lite receiving the domain controllers, firewall, VPN, EDR console, backup platform and ERP, with retention per the P2.9 procedure. Verify clock synchronisation to a single NTP source across all log sources first — unsynchronised clocks quietly invalidate incident evidence. References: ISO A.8.15-A.8.17, VDA ISA chapter 5.

Define a short list of alert-worthy events (admin group changes, repeated failed logons, backup failures, EDR detections, VPN logons from unexpected countries) and wire notifications to the IT lead — small enough to be actually watched by a two-person team.

Maturity level 3 requires the routine, not just the pipe: name the log review owner, set the weekly cadence, and perform the first documented log review within this task, filed as evidence. Manoj verifies end-to-end by generating a test event and showing it arriving centrally with correct timestamp; Masha files the capture for P3.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified logging state) and P1.10 (logging gaps)
- Output of P2.9 (logging and monitoring procedure with retention period)
- Output of P3.3 (final segment layout so collectors reach all sources)
- Access to log sources and the collector with the IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- Log source coverage list with forwarding verification captures in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- NTP configuration evidence and retention configuration export
- First documented log review record; tracker (P0.7) rows updated

### Acceptance criteria

- All agreed sources verifiably forwarding with synchronised timestamps
- Retention matches the P2.9 procedure
- Alert list live and first documented log review filed
- Manoj sign-off on all in-scope rows

issues.name: Remediate & verify backup & recovery + execute restore test
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Two halves, strictly ordered. First, Manoj aligns the backup estate to the P2.9 procedure: scope must cover every production-critical system named in the P2.11 BIA (ERP first — it runs the factory), schedules and retention match the procedure, job success is monitored with failures alerted, and at least one copy is offline, offsite or immutable so ransomware cannot reach it. ISO A.8.13, VDA ISA chapter 5.

Second, execute a real restore test — this is the anchor evidence of the phase. Restore a meaningful target (an ERP database or a file server volume) to an isolated location, time it, verify data integrity with the business owner, and record every step: who, what, source media, duration, outcome versus the RTO/RPO in the BIA. A screenshot of a green job log is not a restore test.

Schedule the restore outside production hours with the IT lead executing and Manoj observing and signing. Masha files the timed record immediately — P3.13 reuses it as the technical leg of the BC/DR exercise, and slippage here cascades into that date.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified backup state) and P1.10 (backup gaps)
- Output of P2.9 (backup procedure) and P2.11 (BIA with RTO/RPO)
- Output of P3.0 (backup storage if procured)
- Restore window agreed with IT lead and business owner

### Outputs / Evidence

- Backup scope-versus-BIA reconciliation and job configuration exports in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Evidence of offline/offsite or immutable copy
- Timed, signed restore test record

### Acceptance criteria

- Every BIA-critical system in backup scope with recent successful runs
- Ransomware-resistant copy verified
- Restore test executed, timed against RTO/RPO, integrity confirmed and signed by Manoj

issues.name: Establish vulnerability & patch management cycle
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Establish a cycle the client can repeat without Underwings, then prove it ran once. Manoj selects the scanning approach (a procured tool via P3.0 or a credible free scanner), defines authenticated scan scope from the P1.9 inventory, and sets patch SLAs by severity in line with the P2.9 procedure — for example critical 14 days, high 30. References: ISO A.8.8, VDA ISA chapter 5.

Run the first full cycle end-to-end as maturity evidence: baseline scan, prioritised finding list, patching by the client IT lead inside a maintenance window agreed with the production manager, then a re-scan demonstrating measurable closure. Servers and the ERP host come first, then clients.

Legacy production-adjacent machines that cannot be patched are handled honestly: isolate them (P3.3), document each as an exception, and record risk acceptance in the risk register (P2.5) with a named owner — an auditor reacts far better to a managed exception than to a hidden one. Manoj signs the cycle record; Masha files scan reports and the exception list, and the recurring cadence feeds the P5.8 client calendar.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory defining scan scope)
- Output of P2.9 (patch management procedure with SLAs)
- Output of P3.0 (scanner licence if procured)
- Maintenance window agreed with IT lead and production manager

### Outputs / Evidence

- Baseline and re-scan reports filed in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Patch cycle record showing prioritisation and closure
- Exception list with risk acceptances; tracker (P0.7) rows updated

### Acceptance criteria

- First scan-patch-rescan cycle completed with evidence of closure
- SLAs documented and cadence scheduled
- All unpatchable systems risk-accepted with compensating controls
- Manoj sign-off

issues.name: Remediate & verify cryptography controls
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Scope this tightly — cryptography for a factory means protecting data at rest and in transit with managed keys, not building a PKI. Manoj verifies and remediates four things: full-disk encryption on all laptops (BitLocker with recovery keys escrowed to AD/Entra, never in a spreadsheet); encryption of backup media and any offsite copies (coordinate with P3.5); TLS with valid certificates on externally reachable services and the ERP web interface; and removal of deprecated protocols where feasible. Governed by the P2.9 key management procedure — ISO A.8.24, VDA ISA chapter 5.

Build a small key and certificate register: what exists, where it lives, who owns it, when it expires. A register with expiry dates is cheap insurance and good ML3 evidence.

Verification is sampled and on-screen: BitLocker status export across the laptop fleet, escrowed key presence for sampled devices, backup encryption settings, certificate details on live services. Masha files exports and the register; Manoj signs. TISAX note: automotive customers expect encrypted handling of drawings and prototypes — align handling rules with P3.9.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.3 (verified crypto findings) and P1.10 (crypto gaps)
- Output of P2.9 (cryptography and key management procedure)
- Output of P1.9 (laptop and server fleet list)
- Console access with the IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- FDE coverage export and sampled key-escrow evidence in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Key and certificate register with owners and expiry dates
- Backup encryption and TLS configuration evidence; tracker (P0.7) rows updated

### Acceptance criteria

- All laptops encrypted with escrowed recovery keys, exceptions risk-accepted
- Backup encryption verified
- Register complete with expiry dates
- Manoj sign-off

issues.name: Remediate & verify physical security controls
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Close every physical gap the P1.4 site walk raised, splitting the work: Manoj verifies technical measures, Masha builds the operating processes and briefs the people running them. Priority order: server room (restricted key/badge list, access log, door actually locking, no cardboard against the racks), then site entry (gate visitor log, badges, escort rule, contractor handling), then CCTV (coverage of entries and server room, retention verified on the recorder), then environmental — in a tannery check server-room AC against heat and humidity, plus UPS and fire response. References: ISO A.7, VDA ISA chapter 3.

TISAX raises the bar on customer-owned material — drawings, samples, prototype leather parts — which needs a designated protected storage area with controlled access; that is exactly what the assessment provider probes.

Brief gate guards and reception in the languages they actually speak, and run the new visitor process live for several days before sampling. Purchased items trace back to P3.0 — chase them there. Masha files before/after photos, access lists, visitor log samples and CCTV retention screenshots; Manoj signs.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.4 (site walk findings) and P1.10 (physical gaps)
- Output of P2.13 (physical security policy) and P3.0 (delivered hardware)
- Facilities counterpart and guard/reception staff availability

### Outputs / Evidence

- Before/after photos, server-room access list and log samples in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Visitor log samples and CCTV retention evidence
- Tracker (P0.7) A.7 and ISA chapter 3 rows updated

### Acceptance criteria

- All P1.4 findings closed or formally risk-accepted
- Server-room access list minimal and logged
- Visitor process operating with filed samples
- CCTV retention verified and signed off by Manoj

issues.name: Operationalise asset management & media handling
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha turns the P1.9 snapshot into a living asset management practice. First, make the inventory operational: every asset row has a named owner, a classification per the P2.13 scheme, and a lifecycle status; agree with the IT lead who updates it and when, tied to the P3.1 JML process so joiners and leavers touch the register. References: ISO A.5.9-A.5.14, A.7.10, A.7.14; VDA ISA chapter 1 asset requirements.
