Second, apply labelling pragmatically: physical labels on hardware, classification markings on document templates, and handling rules per class published where staff can find them. In a multilingual factory, a one-page pictorial handling guide beats a policy PDF.

Third, operationalise media handling and disposal: removable media rules enforced technically via the P3.2 USB controls, a wipe/destruction procedure with a disposal certificate template, and — if equipment or media is retired during the window — a first completed disposal record as ML3 evidence. Manoj spot-checks sampled assets against the register and countersigns; register and samples feed the P3.15 asset-theme pack.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.9 (asset inventory with owners and classification)
- Output of P2.13 (classification and handling policy)
- Output of P3.1 (JML process to hook register updates into)
- Output of P3.2 (USB device control configuration)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed living asset register with owner and update process in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Labelling samples (photos) and published handling rules
- Disposal procedure, certificate template and first disposal record if applicable

### Acceptance criteria

- Register complete, owned and signed with update triggers defined
- Sampled assets labelled and matching the register
- Media and disposal procedures operating, with first records where applicable
- Manoj spot-check countersignature

issues.name: Operationalise HR security controls with records
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha closes the record gaps P1.6 found, working with the HR counterpart. Four record sets matter: signed confidentiality/NDA undertakings for every employee and long-term contractor; pre-employment screening evidence within UAE practice (identity and right-to-work via passport/visa records held by the PRO, reference checks for sensitive roles); security responsibilities written into contracts or job descriptions; and live onboarding/offboarding checklists wired to the P3.1 JML process so account actions and asset returns (P3.9) are evidenced per person. References: ISO A.6.1-A.6.6, VDA ISA chapter 2.

For the existing workforce, run a catch-up NDA campaign: short bilingual (English/Arabic, plus workforce languages where needed) undertakings, signed during shift briefings — Masha coordinates with the production manager to reach all shifts, and keeps a signature log against the HR roster to prove 100% coverage.

Confirm the disciplinary process references security breaches (A.6.4) and that offboarding actually triggered for any leaver during the window — that one completed record is the theme's strongest ML3 evidence. Manoj reviews the record set and countersigns; everything files to the HR-theme pack for P3.15.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.6 (HR control findings) and P2.13 (HR policy bundle)
- Output of P3.1 (JML process) and HR roster
- HR counterpart and production manager for shift access

### Outputs / Evidence

- NDA signature log reconciled to the HR roster in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Screening evidence samples for recent hires
- Completed onboarding/offboarding checklist records

### Acceptance criteria

- 100% NDA coverage evidenced against the roster
- Checklists in live use with at least one completed record each
- Screening approach documented and evidenced for recent hires
- Manoj countersignature on the record set

issues.name: Embed supplier security: issue clauses & assess key suppliers
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha operationalises the P2.12 supplier framework against real suppliers. From the supplier register, confirm the key-supplier shortlist with procurement: the IT MSP and ERP vendor, machinery vendors holding remote-maintenance access (cross-check P3.3 findings), chemical suppliers, logistics providers handling customer goods, and any cloud services. References: ISO A.5.19-A.5.22, VDA ISA chapter 6.

This is a **Client-Action** task: the client procurement counterpart issues the security clauses/addenda and the self-assessment questionnaires on client letterhead; Masha drafts everything, tracks despatch and returns, and chases weekly. Set a return deadline that leaves a week for assessment before the 09-04 due date — UAE suppliers respond slowly to unfamiliar paperwork, so a short phone briefing from procurement alongside the email lifts response rates.

Masha performs first-pass assessment of returns; Manoj reviews the risk ratings and any supplier that refuses or fails. Ratings and residual risks land in the supplier register and, where material, the risk register (P2.5). Non-responders are escalated to the sponsor at the weekly call — an evidenced chase trail itself demonstrates the process operates.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.12 (supplier security policy, register and contract clauses)
- Output of P3.3 (vendors with remote-maintenance access)
- Procurement counterpart to issue clauses and questionnaires
- Supplier contact details from the client

### Outputs / Evidence

- Issued clauses/addenda and questionnaire despatch log in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Completed questionnaire returns with assessment notes
- Updated supplier register with risk ratings; escalation notes for non-responders

### Acceptance criteria

- Clauses issued to all key suppliers with despatch evidence
- Returns from top suppliers assessed and risk-rated by Manoj review
- Register updated; non-responders escalated with a documented chase trail

issues.name: Run incident response tabletop exercise
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj designs and facilitates a 90-120 minute tabletop that exercises the P2.10 incident procedure with the people who would actually run it: IT lead, ISMS owner, production manager, HR and a management representative. Pick a scenario the room believes: ransomware on the ERP server mid-shift, or phishing-led credential theft spreading to the file server. Prepare two or three escalating injects (backups suspected encrypted, an automotive customer requests status, a journalist calls). References: ISO A.5.24-A.5.27, VDA ISA chapter 1 incident management.

Walk the full lifecycle — detect, classify, contain, communicate, recover, learn — and force the uncomfortable decisions: who authorises shutting down production, who informs automotive customers (TISAX participants are expected to notify affected partners), what gets reported under UAE requirements, who talks to the press. Masha scribes decisions and gaps verbatim and captures attendance.

Close with a debrief and produce an exercise report: scenario, participants, timeline, what worked, what failed, and actions with owners and dates. Feed procedure fixes back into P2.10 as a version update — an exercised, corrected procedure is what ML3 looks like. Report and attendance file to the P3.15 incident-theme pack.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.10 (approved incident response procedure)
- Output of P3.4 (logging/alerting state, for realistic detection discussion)
- Participant availability across a shift-compatible slot
- Scenario and inject pack prepared by Manoj

### Outputs / Evidence

- Exercise report with timeline, findings and actions in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Attendance record signed by participants
- Updated incident procedure version reflecting lessons

### Acceptance criteria

- Exercise executed with all key roles attending
- Report filed with lessons and owned actions
- Procedure updated and re-published where gaps were found

issues.name: Run BC/DR exercise (tabletop + restore-linked)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj runs the business-continuity exercise as a tabletop anchored to real data — the timed restore record from P3.5 is the technical backbone, so this task must follow it. Scenario: server-room loss or a destructive incident taking down ERP and file services on a production day. Participants: production manager, IT lead, ISMS owner, facilities and a management representative. References: ISO A.5.29-A.5.30, VDA ISA continuity requirements in chapters 3 and 5.

Walk the P2.11 plan end-to-end: invocation decision and authority, communication tree (including automotive customers), manual workarounds keeping production and despatch moving while IT recovers, and recovery sequence. Then hold the plan against reality: compare BIA RTO/RPO assumptions with the measured P3.5 restore duration. Where measurement beats assumption, update the plan; where it misses, improve the setup or have management accept the longer RTO in writing.

Masha scribes and captures attendance. Output is an exercise report plus a red-lined P2.11 update — a plan validated against a real restore is strong evidence at both the ISO audit and TISAX assessment. Actions with owners go on the log; everything files to the P3.15 continuity pack.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.11 (BC/DR plan with BIA) and P3.5 (timed restore test record)
- Output of P3.12 (exercise format lessons, if already run)
- Participant availability including the production manager

### Outputs / Evidence

- BC/DR exercise report with RTO/RPO validation in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Signed attendance record
- Updated BC/DR plan version with measured recovery data

### Acceptance criteria

- Exercise held with production, IT and management present
- RTO/RPO validated against the P3.5 restore evidence or formally re-accepted
- Plan updated and actions logged with owners

issues.name: Remediate mobile device & teleworking controls
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj and Masha split this: Manoj enforces the technical controls, Masha lands the paperwork and user acknowledgements. Scope per the P2.13 telework and mobile policy: corporate laptops and phones enrolled into MDM or an equivalent managed baseline (screen lock, encryption via P3.7, remote wipe), remote access only through the P3.3 VPN with MFA, and an explicit documented BYOD position. References: ISO A.6.7, A.8.1; VDA ISA mobile-work requirements in chapters 2 and 5.

Be realistic about UAE factory habits: WhatsApp on personal phones is the default business channel with drivers, suppliers and shift leads. Do not pretend it away — define what may and may not be shared through it (no customer drawings, credentials or personal data), put that in the acknowledgement, and offer a managed alternative for anything classified.

Prove enforcement, not intent: export the MDM enrolment list and diff it against the P1.9 device inventory, and run a remote-wipe test on one spare device, recording the result. Masha collects signed acknowledgements from all device holders and reconciles against the P3.9 asset register. Exceptions are risk-accepted; Manoj signs.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.13 (telework and mobile policy) and P1.9 (device inventory)
- Output of P3.3 (VPN with MFA) and P3.7 (device encryption)
- Output of P3.0 (MDM licences if procured)

### Outputs / Evidence

- MDM enrolment export reconciled to the device inventory in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Remote-wipe test record
- Signed user acknowledgements reconciled to device holders

### Acceptance criteria

- All corporate mobile devices and laptops enrolled or risk-accepted exceptions
- Remote wipe demonstrated on one device
- Acknowledgements on file for every device holder
- Manoj sign-off

issues.name: Compile per-theme implemented-evidence packs
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha assembles one evidence pack per control theme — IAM, endpoint, network, logging, backup/restore, vulnerability management, cryptography, physical, asset/media, HR, supplier, incident, continuity, mobile/telework — mirroring the P3.1-P3.14 task structure. Each pack follows a fixed order: governing policy or procedure (version and approval date), implementation evidence (configs, exports, photos, records), verification record, and Manoj's sign-off, with consistent naming (`theme_artifact_date`) and an index sheet.

Build packs against the dual-mapped tracker (P0.7): every Annex A row and VDA ISA requirement marked implemented must link to a pack artifact. The dual mapping is the payoff — one pack serves both the ISO audit and the TISAX AL2 assessment, where evidence is reviewed remotely via web conference and must stand on its own.

Work incrementally as P3 tasks close; chase evidence-owing tasks the moment they mark done and escalate anything missing to Manoj at the weekly call. Rows with no linkable evidence are flagged honestly — they feed the P3.16 re-score and, if unresolved, the P4.6 internal audit rather than surprising the external assessment.

### Inputs

- Outputs of P3.1 through P3.14 (verification evidence and sign-offs)
- Output of P0.7 (dual-mapped control tracker) and P0.6 (repository structure)
- Phase 2 approved policies and procedures (P2.8-P2.14, approved at P2.15)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Fourteen indexed per-theme evidence packs in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Tracker rows hyperlinked to pack artifacts
- Missing-evidence flag list handed to P3.16

### Acceptance criteria

- One indexed pack exists per theme with the fixed internal structure
- Every implemented tracker row links to at least one artifact
- Every pack contains Manoj's sign-off
- Missing-evidence list issued to P3.16 and raised at the weekly call

issues.name: Re-score VDA ISA to ML3 and update SoA/tracker post-remediation
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj re-runs the full VDA ISA 6.0 self-assessment from P1.7 against the remediated estate. Score every requirement with a direct reference to P3.15 pack evidence — a score without an evidence pointer does not count. Target is ML3: a defined, documented process demonstrably operating, which is why Phase 3 insisted on first-cycle records (access reviews, log review, restore test, exercises) rather than screenshots alone.

Score honestly — the AL2 provider tests plausibility in interviews and remote evidence review, and inflation converts directly into findings. Where a requirement sits below ML3, record why plus the closing action; this residual gap list feeds the P4.5 internal audit scope and the P5.1 close-out, with the final submission score landing at P5.2.

In the same pass update the SoA (P2.7): implementation status moves to implemented-verified where the tracker row is signed, justifications current (clause 6.1.3 d). Version both documents; Masha files them with a change note against the P1.7 baseline so the delta is visible at W7 and the P4.9 review.

### Inputs

- Output of P1.7 (baseline ISA scores) and P3.15 (evidence packs and flag list)
- Output of P0.7 (signed tracker rows) and P2.7 (SoA v1)
- Outputs of P3.1-P3.14 (sign-off status per theme)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Re-scored VDA ISA workbook with evidence references in the evidence repository (P0.6)
- Updated, versioned SoA
- Residual gap list with owners and dates, issued to P4.5 and P5.1

### Acceptance criteria

- Every ISA requirement re-scored with an evidence reference
- No sub-ML3 score without a documented reason and closing action
- SoA updated, versioned and consistent with the tracker
- Delta versus P1.7 baseline reported at the weekly call

issues.name: Produce awareness training materials (ISO + TISAX, factory-adapted)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha builds the awareness materials directly from the approved and published policy set (P2.15) — clause 7.3 requires staff to know the policy, their contribution and the consequences of nonconformity, and VDA ISA 2.1.3 expects demonstrably trained, aware staff. Two formats: a 30-40 minute deck for office and IT staff, and a 10-15 minute toolbox-talk pack for the shop floor with poster one-pagers for noticeboards.

Content priorities for this factory: classification and handling of automotive-customer drawings and specifications (top tier per P2.13), the incident reporting route including the phone-and-supervisor channel from P2.10, acceptable use, visitor and escort rules, and clear desk and clear screen. The workforce is multilingual: write a plain-English master, add translated summaries in the main workforce languages, and prefer pictograms over text on posters.

Add a five-question quiz and a sign-in sheet template so P4.2 produces attendance and effectiveness evidence by design. Manoj reviews for technical accuracy; finish by 09-08 so sessions start immediately.

### Inputs

- Approved policy set from P2.15, especially the P2.13 bundle and the P2.10 incident procedure
- Communication channels defined in P0.5 (supervisors and noticeboards for the shop floor)
- Awareness objective and metric from the P2.2 objectives register
- Workforce language mix and shift roster from HR (P0.8)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Office deck and shop-floor toolbox-talk pack filed under the clause-7 and ISA chapter-2 folders
- Translated noticeboard one-pagers
- Quiz with answer key and attendance sheet template handed to P4.2

### Acceptance criteria

- Materials cover policy obligations, incident reporting, classification and consequences of nonconformity
- Shop-floor variant exists with translated summaries
- Quiz and attendance templates ready for P4.2
- Manoj technical review complete

issues.name: Deliver all-staff awareness sessions with attendance records
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Deliver awareness to the entire in-scope workforce, not just office staff — both auditors sample attendance against the roster. Masha schedules with HR around the shift pattern: several short toolbox talks at shift handovers for production crews, one or two longer sessions for office and IT staff. Supervisors gather their crews — the Client-Action here: HR and production management own turnout. Manoj co-delivers and takes the questions on incident reporting and customer-data handling; Masha runs registration and the quiz.

Capture a signed attendance sheet per session and reconcile daily against the HR roster. Absentees — night shift, leave, new joiners — get a dated catch-up session: coverage percentage is the number an auditor asks for, not sessions held. Target at least 95 percent by 09-10 with the remainder booked.

File scans the same day and summarise quiz results anonymously. These records evidence clause 7.3 and the P2.2 training objective, and the internal audit (P4.6) will sample them, so file cleanly under the P0.6 conventions.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.1 (materials, quiz, sign-in templates)
- Refreshed HR roster and shift schedule (P0.8 baseline)
- Supervisor and noticeboard channels from P0.5
- Rooms and time slots confirmed by the P0.1 counterparts

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed attendance sheets per session, scanned and filed under clause-7 and ISA chapter-2
- Coverage reconciliation against the roster with dated catch-up plan
- Anonymised quiz results summary handed to P4.8

### Acceptance criteria

- Sessions delivered for office staff and every production shift
- Attendance records filed for every session
- Coverage at least 95 percent with the remainder booked with dates
- Quiz results recorded and passed to P4.8

issues.name: Deliver role-based training for IT admins & incident responders
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Clause 7.2 competence for the people who operate the ISMS daily. Manoj trains the client IT lead and admins hands-on at the consoles on the procedures they now own: JML and privileged access per P2.8 as implemented in P3.1, backup and restore per P2.9 and the P3.5 test, log triage and alert handling from P3.4, and the patch cycle from P3.6. Incident responders — the incident manager and deputy named in the P2.1 RACI — walk the P2.10 procedure end to end: severity classification, evidence preservation, customer notification, folding in lessons from the P3.12 tabletop.

Format is runbook walkthrough plus demonstration, never slides: each trainee performs a real task — verify a restore log, execute the leaver checklist, classify a sample incident — and the demonstration is written into the competence record. That practised element is what lifts VDA ISA chapter 2 maturity to level 3.

Masha maintains the training matrix mapping each role to required competences and records gaps; anyone missing gets a dated follow-up before the P5.9 handover session.

### Inputs

- Approved procedures from P2.8, P2.9 and P2.10
- Exercise reports from P3.12 and P3.13
- Named admins and responders from the P2.1 operating RACI
- Console access alongside the client IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- Per-person role-based training and competence records filed under clause-7 and ISA chapter-2
- Training matrix mapping roles to competences, gaps flagged

### Acceptance criteria

- Every named admin and responder trained with a dated record
- Each record includes a demonstrated task, not attendance alone
- Training matrix complete with follow-ups dated
- Records available to the P4.6 audit sample

issues.name: Run phishing simulation and record results
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

The simulation measures whether P4.2 changed behaviour, so run it after the sessions, not before — the result then reads as post-training performance for clause 9.1 and the effectiveness angle of VDA ISA 2.1.3. Masha obtains written sponsor authorisation first and agrees the scope: email users only, which at this factory means office, IT and supervisory staff.

Coordinate quietly with the client IT lead to whitelist the sending domain so the mail gateway does not swallow the campaign and the result measures people. Use a plausible generic lure such as a supplier invoice or an HR announcement; never imitate the real automotive customer, a bank or a UAE authority. Measure delivery, click rate, credential entry, and — the number that matters most — reports made through the P2.10 channel.

Publish aggregate, anonymised results only. Individual clickers get quiet re-training, never discipline; agree this no-blame rule with HR up front, which also keeps the exercise clean under UAE PDPL. Hand results to P4.8 for the management review and record them against the P2.2 awareness objective.

### Inputs

- Written sponsor authorisation for the campaign
- Email-user list from the client IT lead
- Output of P4.2 (sessions completed)
- Incident reporting channel live per P2.10
- Simulation tooling agreed with client IT

### Outputs / Evidence

- Authorisation record and campaign configuration evidence
- Aggregate results report (delivery, click, credential and report rates) filed under clause-9 and ISA chapter-2

### Acceptance criteria

- Written authorisation filed before launch
- Campaign executed to the agreed scope with gateway whitelisting confirmed
- Aggregate results recorded with no individual names
- Results delivered to P4.8

issues.name: Prepare internal audit programme, plan & checklist (cl 9.2)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Two documents. The audit programme (clause 9.2.2) is written for the client's future: a rolling annual cycle covering clauses 4-10 and every SoA-applicable Annex A theme, methods, responsibilities and reporting — the client must be able to rerun it without consultants, which is what VDA ISA 1.5.1 maturity expects. The audit plan covers this engagement's audit, fieldwork 09-10 to 09-15: full-ISMS scope, criteria (ISO 27001:2022, the approved document set, VDA ISA 6.0 at target ML3), an interview schedule per function that respects shift patterns, and the technical sampling approach.

Handle independence explicitly: neither auditor audits their own work. Manoj audits the documentation and records areas Masha authored; Masha, under Manoj's direction, audits records of technical controls Manoj implemented and verified. A two-person consultancy cannot achieve full separation, so document the objectivity measures in the programme — the certification body will probe this.

Build the checklist from the P0.7 tracker and the clause structure so every line traces to a requirement. Masha issues auditee notifications with dates and times via the P0.5 channels.

### Inputs

- SoA from P2.7 and the dual-mapped tracker from P0.7
- Approved document set (P2.15) and evidence packs (P3.15)
- Re-score results from P3.16
- House audit programme, plan and checklist templates

### Outputs / Evidence

- Audit programme v1.0 and audit plan filed under clause-9
- Audit checklist traceable to tracker rows
- Auditee notification record

### Acceptance criteria

- Programme covers a full annual cycle with the independence rationale documented
- Plan schedules all functions and technical sampling within 09-10 to 09-15
- Every checklist line traces to a clause or control requirement
- Auditees notified via P0.5 channels

issues.name: Conduct internal ISMS audit (documents, interviews, technical sampling)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Execute the P4.5 plan over three to four days the way the certification body and the TISAX assessor will: document review, interviews, technical sampling. Document review tests that the clause 4-10 set operates — records exist and versions are controlled per P2.14. Interviews revisit the P1.2 owners — sponsor, ISMS owner, IT, HR, production, procurement — but now test operation: show me the last access review, the last incident, this week's backup check. Technical sampling re-verifies a slice of Phase 3 at the console: one JML case end to end, a restore log, an access review record, a patch report, plus a floor walk for physical controls and clear desk.

Record objective evidence per checklist line — what was seen, where filed, conform or not. Classify findings major NC, minor NC or OFI as encountered, and run a daily wrap-up with auditees so the P4.7 report surprises nobody. Keep to the P4.5 independence split throughout.

This doubles as the client's rehearsal for Stage 1 and the AL2 interviews — coach counterparts to answer with evidence, not narrative.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.5 (plan, checklist, notifications)
- Evidence packs (P3.15) and evidence register (P1.8)
- Auditee availability per schedule
- Console and site access with the client IT lead

### Outputs / Evidence

- Completed checklists with per-line evidence references
- Interview, sampling and daily wrap-up notes filed under clause-9
- Raw findings list handed to P4.7

### Acceptance criteria

- Every planned area audited or deviation recorded against the plan
- Every checklist line closed with evidence reference and conclusion
- Findings communicated to auditees during fieldwork
- Raw findings delivered to P4.7 on 09-15

issues.name: Issue internal audit report + nonconformity & corrective-action log
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj issues the report within one working day of fieldwork ending: scope, criteria, dates, auditors and the independence note, a conformity summary by clause and theme, then the findings — each with its objective evidence reference, classification (major NC, minor NC, OFI) and the clause or control it breaches. Resist softening: an internal audit with no findings is itself a credibility finding at Stage 1, and the corrective-action trail is exactly what clause 10.2 and maturity level 3 want demonstrated.

Open the nonconformity and corrective-action log alongside. Per NC: description, root cause — facilitated with the responsible client owner, not written for them — correction, corrective action, named client owner, and a due date no later than 09-22 so P5.1 can verify closure inside the window. OFIs are logged separately as options, never commitments.

Masha files everything, links each finding to its P0.7 tracker row, and distributes to the sponsor and auditees. Results are presented to management via P4.8 and P4.9.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.6 (checklists, notes, raw findings)
- Tracker P0.7 for finding-to-control links
- CA log template per the P2.14 conventions
- Root-cause input from responsible client owners

### Outputs / Evidence

- Internal audit report v1.0 filed under clause-9
- Live NC and corrective-action log filed under clause-10 and linked to P5.1
- Distribution record to sponsor and auditees

### Acceptance criteria

- Report issued and distributed by 09-16
- Every NC has root cause, corrective action, named owner and a due date on or before 09-22
- OFIs logged separately from NCs
- Findings linked to tracker rows

issues.name: Prepare management review input pack (cl 9.3 inputs)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Masha assembles every clause 9.3.2 input so the meeting decides instead of reads. Cover in order: status of previous review actions — first review, so record none and state the baseline; changes in internal and external issues since P2.1; interested-party changes; performance against the P2.2 objectives with measured values — training coverage from P4.2, phishing results from P4.4, the P3.5 restore test, the P3.12 and P3.13 exercises, patch SLA, ML3 status from P3.16; monitoring results; internal audit results and CA status from P4.7; risk assessment results and treatment plan status (P2.5, P2.6); resource needs; improvement opportunities; and the outlook into Phase 6 — the confirmed audit bookings (P5.3, P5.4) and the upcoming ENX submission (P5.2) that open the assessment window.

Format as a short deck plus a one-page dashboard, each item ending with the decision required from management. Where an input is nil, say so explicitly with the reason — silent omissions become audit findings.

Manoj reviews content before release; circulate to attendees at least 24 hours ahead of P4.9 via the P0.5 channels.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.7 (audit report and CA log)
- P2.2 objectives register with measured results
- Risk register and treatment plan status (P2.5, P2.6) after the P3.16 re-score
- P4.2 coverage figures and P4.4 aggregate results
- Weekly minutes W1-W15 for trend context

### Outputs / Evidence

- Management review input pack filed under clause-9
- Circulation record showing 24-hour advance distribution

### Acceptance criteria

- Every clause 9.3.2 input addressed or explicitly nil with a reason
- Objectives reported with measured values, not status words
- Decision-required list included per item
- Pack circulated at least 24 hours before P4.9

issues.name: Facilitate management review meeting + signed minutes
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Manoj chairs with the sponsor and management team; Masha books it via P0.5, scribes, and captures decisions verbatim. Walk the P4.8 pack and force the clause 9.3.3 outputs into the record: continual-improvement decisions, ISMS changes, and resources. Specifically obtain four things — confirmation of corrective-action owners and dates for every P4.7 nonconformity, acceptance or re-treatment of residual risks above appetite from P2.5, endorsement of the ML3 posture for the P5.2 ENX submission, and ratification of the bookings (P5.3, P5.4) plus the go for the Phase 6 assessment window, fees acknowledged as client-paid.

Minutes record decisions and actions with owner and date, not discussion. The sponsor signs the same day: signed minutes are mandatory clause 9.3 evidence, the CB will not run Stage 1 (P6.2) without a completed management review, and they double as clause 5.1 leadership and VDA ISA 1.2 commitment evidence for the TISAX assessor.

Masha files the minutes and transfers every action into the CA log and the project board so P5.1 inherits a single closure list. Report completion at the W16 gate call on 2026-11-13.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.8 (pack circulated 24 hours ahead)
- Sponsor and management availability booked via P0.5
- CA log from P4.7 and risk register from P2.5
- ISA re-score results from P3.16

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed management review minutes filed under clause-9
- Decision and action list with owners and dates
- Updated CA log handed to P5.1

### Acceptance criteria

- All clause 9.3.2 inputs covered and 9.3.3 outputs minuted
- Every action carries a named owner and date
- Sponsor signature obtained same day (2026-11-12)
- Actions transferred to P5.1 and the board

issues.name: Close corrective actions from internal audit & ISA re-score
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

The P4.7 nonconformity and corrective-action log is the single workset; it already merges internal audit findings with the sub-ML3 residuals from P3.16. Take majors first. Per item, confirm root cause with the client owner, implement the correction and corrective action, then run an **effectiveness check** — evidence the fix works, not just that it was done: a repeated access-review sample, a fresh scan, a re-inspection photo.

Manoj re-verifies every technical closure at console or site level and signs the P0.7 tracker row before the log entry moves to closed — the Phase 3 verify-first rule. Masha updates the log daily, chases owners, and files closure evidence beside the original finding so an auditor can follow finding, root cause, action and effectiveness in one chain — the trail ISO clause 10.2 and a VDA ISA ML3 assessor sample.

Items that cannot close by 09-22 (typically procurement-dependent) get a dated action plan, a named client owner and written sponsor acknowledgment, and carry into the P5.7 open-items log and P5.8 calendar. Nothing is silently dropped.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.7 (NC and corrective-action log, including P3.16 residuals)
- Output of P4.9 (management review decisions)
- Tracker P0.7 with evidence links
- Client owners available per log entry

### Outputs / Evidence

- Final corrective-action log filed under clause-10
- Closure evidence per item linked from tracker rows
- Sponsor acknowledgments for dated residual actions

### Acceptance criteria

- Zero open major nonconformities at 09-22
- Every minor closed with an effectiveness check, or scheduled with dated action, owner and sponsor acknowledgment
- Manoj signature on every technical closure
- Log and tracker consistent; residuals carried into the P5.7 open-items log

issues.name: Finalise VDA ISA self-assessment for audit-provider submission
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Produce the final VDA ISA 6.0 self-assessment for lodgement with the audit provider. Start from the P3.16 v2 scoring, then update every requirement touched by a P5.1 closure. Score strictly from verified evidence: the AL2 assessment is a plausibility check of exactly this file, and inflated maturity claims are the fastest route to failure. Target ML3 per Information Security module requirement, including high-protection extras where scoped.

Manoj cross-checks each score against the P3.15 evidence packs and the P0.7 tracker — inconsistency between workbook and evidence is the classic AL2 finding. Complete the workbook company and scope tabs using the P0.2 scope wording registered at ENX, so the assessor sees one identical scope everywhere.

Confirm with the provider booked in P5.3 whether they want the native VDA ISA Excel or a portal upload, and deliver in that format. Close with a one-page scoring-basis memo stating the evidence cut-off date and where residual sub-ML3 items are owned, then walk the sponsor through and obtain signature.

### Inputs

- Output of P3.16 (ISA scoring v2)
- Output of P5.1 (closures affecting scores)
- Outputs of P3.15 (evidence packs) and tracker P0.7
- P0.2 scope text and P0.3 scoping memo
- Provider format requirements from P5.3

### Outputs / Evidence

- Final VDA ISA self-assessment, versioned, filed in the TISAX section
- Scoring-basis memo
- Lodgement record with the audit provider

### Acceptance criteria

- Every IS-module requirement scored; ML3 met or residual owned in the corrective-action log
- Scores consistent with evidence packs and tracker, cross-check signed by Manoj
- Signed by the sponsor and lodged with client and audit provider in the required format

issues.name: Select ENX-listed audit provider and book TISAX AL2 assessment
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

11-06 is the confirmation deadline, not the start: RFQs went out by 2026-10-05; TISAX assessor calendars book out 4 to 12 weeks. Shortlist ENX-listed providers active in the UAE/GCC (TUV Rheinland, TUV SUD, DEKRA, DQS) and collect two comparable quotes for an **AL2 assessment, Information Security module**, matching the P0.2 scope text exactly.

AL2 is normally a remote plausibility check of the P5.2 self-assessment, so clarify per bidder: interview format, working language, evidence sampling, fees, and a slot inside the Phase 6 window (2026-11-23 to 2027-01-29). Masha runs comparison sheet and correspondence; Manoj checks quoted scope and level against the P0.3 memo before signature.

Contracting and payment are **Client-Action**: Underwings coordinates but cannot contract, so get the engagement letter to the sponsor early. Once signed, the client links the assessment to the participant scope in the ENX portal (P0.4) and confirms the date. Capture format and dates for P5.9, P6.1 and the P6.4 assessment Manoj hosts.

### Inputs

- Output of P0.4 (participant ID and portal access)
- P0.2 scope statement and P0.3 scoping memo (AL2, IS module, ML3)
- RFQ responses (issued by 10-05)
- Client budget approval and signatory

### Outputs / Evidence

- Quote comparison sheet (two or more ENX-listed providers), filed in the bookings section
- Signed provider engagement and assessment date confirmation
- ENX portal screenshot of the assessment linked to the correct scope

### Acceptance criteria

- At least two ENX-listed provider quotes compared and filed
- Provider contracted by the client; AL2 date confirmed inside the Phase 6 window
- Assessment date visible against the correct scope in the ENX portal
- Date and format fed into P5.9, P6.1 and P6.4

issues.name: Select ISO certification body and book Stage 1 audit
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Mirror of P5.3 on the ISO side, on the same external-calendar logic: RFQs out by 2026-10-05, confirmation by 11-06. Collect three quotes from certification bodies **accredited for ISO/IEC 27001** by a recognised accreditation body (EIAC, UKAS or DAkkS are common in the UAE) — verify the accreditation scope actually covers ISO/IEC 27001:2022, otherwise the certificate is worthless to the client's automotive customers. Ask each CB to price the full three-year cycle: Stage 1, Stage 2 and two surveillance audits, with man-days per IAF MD 5 from headcount and scope.

Masha normalises quotes into a comparison sheet and handles correspondence. Manoj writes a one-page recommendation memo comparing accreditation, auditor availability in the UAE, manufacturing-sector experience, language and cost — the client decides and contracts directly; CB fees are client-paid, outside the Underwings engagement.

Book Stage 1 early in the Phase 6 window (placeholder ~2026-12-09, pinned when the CB confirms — P6.2); pencil Stage 2 for ~2027-01-13 (P6.6) so Stage 1 findings close between them (P6.3). Confirm remote or on-site and record logistics for P5.9 and the P6.2/P6.6 hosting Manoj leads.

### Inputs

- P0.2 scope statement (drives audit-day calculation)
- RFQ responses from three accredited CBs (issued by 10-05)
- Client budget approval and signatory for the CB contract

### Outputs / Evidence

- Three-quote comparison sheet and Manoj recommendation memo, filed in the bookings section
- Signed CB agreement and Stage 1 booking confirmation
- Provisional Stage 2 window recorded

### Acceptance criteria

- Three accredited CB quotes compared; recommendation memo delivered
- Stage 1 date confirmed in writing inside the Phase 6 window; Stage 2 provisionally scheduled
- Client written acknowledgment that CB fees are client-paid

issues.name: Run pre-assessment readiness walkthrough (mock Stage 1 / TISAX dry run)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Half-day mock assessment with Manoj playing the external auditor. The client ISMS owner and IT lead answer; coaching happens only in the debrief — at the real Stage 1 and AL2 interview consultants can at most observe, so the session proves the client can defend the ISMS unaided.

Use a 15-question sample spanning both frameworks: scope and context, policy and objectives, risk methodology and register, SoA, incident process, access reviews, backup and restore proof, internal audit, management review, corrective actions. Phrase TISAX questions against ISA chapters 1 to 5, and add three navigation drills: from a P0.7 tracker row to its filed evidence in under two minutes, live on screen. Factory touch: have the ISMS owner explain visitor and shop-floor controls as if walking an auditor through the plant.

Score each answer pass, coach or fail; debrief immediately and re-drill fails the same day. Masha logs results and feeds unresolved weak spots into the P5.9 focus list. Running on 09-23, before the P5.7 pack freezes, means navigation problems surfaced here can still be fixed in the pack.

### Inputs

- Output of P5.1 (corrective actions closed)
- Output of P5.6 (documentation checklist verified)
- Tracker P0.7 and P3.15 evidence packs
- Client ISMS owner and IT lead booked for a half day

### Outputs / Evidence

- Question set with per-question scoring, filed under clause-9
- Debrief note listing re-drilled items and residual weak spots
- Focus list handed to P5.9

### Acceptance criteria

- Client answers the 15-question sample without prompting
- All three evidence-navigation drills completed unaided within two minutes each
- Fails re-drilled same day; residual weak spots on the P5.9 focus list

issues.name: Verify mandatory documented information checklist complete
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Audit the P2.14 master document register line by line against the full ISO/IEC 27001:2022 mandatory documented information list: scope (4.3), information security policy (5.2), risk assessment process and results (6.1.2, 8.2), risk treatment process, plan and results (6.1.3, 8.3), the Statement of Applicability, objectives (6.2), evidence of competence (7.2), operational planning and control (8.1), monitoring and measurement results (9.1), internal audit programme and results (9.2), management review results (9.3), and nonconformities with corrective actions (10.2).

Verify four things per item: latest version exists; approved and signed per the P2.14 document-control procedure; filed at the location the register states; register metadata (version, owner, approval date) matches the file. Rate each row green, amber or red. Ambers (a stale version number, a moved file) are fixed on the spot with Masha; reds escalate same day — this checklist is the ISO-side gate before the P5.7 pack freeze.

Manoj countersigns the completed checklist. TISAX has no equivalent mandatory list, but nearly every item doubles as ISA chapter 1 evidence, so file it where both assessors will find it.

### Inputs

- Output of P2.14 (master document register)
- Output of P5.1 (updated 10.2 records)
- Signed policy stack from P2.15; SoA from P3.16
- Read access to the full evidence repository

### Outputs / Evidence

- Completed mandatory-documentation checklist, countersigned by Manoj, filed under clause-7
- Corrected register entries where mismatches were found

### Acceptance criteria

- Every mandatory item rated green — present, approved, correctly filed, register-accurate
- Checklist countersigned by Manoj by 09-22
- Any corrections applied to the register same day

issues.name: Compile final handover pack + evidence index
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Assemble the single pack an external auditor could work from cold — the P6.1 submission base for the P6.2 and P6.4 audits — structured on the P0.6 repository taxonomy. Contents: master document register (post-P5.6), final P0.7 dual-mapped tracker, evidence index merging P1.8 and P3.15, risk register and treatment plan (P2.5, P2.6), signed SoA (post-P3.16), internal audit and management review records (P4.5 to P4.9), final ISA scoring (P5.2), booking confirmations (P5.3, P5.4), and the P5.1 open-items log.

Add a **credential and access transfer sheet**: every account, portal and repository Underwings holds — ENX portal included — with a handover action per item; Underwings keeps only what Phase 6 hosting needs, removal executing at final closure (P6.10), client confirming receipt. Masha compiles, fixes dead links, and freezes the pack as v1.0 read-only with a table of contents.

Quality gate is cold-handability: Manoj picks ten random tracker rows and follows each to its evidence within a minute, unassisted. Failures go back to Masha same day; rerun on fresh rows until clean.

### Inputs

- Outputs of P5.1, P5.2, P5.6 (closed CA log, final ISA scoring, verified register)
- Booking confirmations (P5.3, P5.4)
- Tracker P0.7, evidence packs P3.15, risk register P2.5
- List of all Underwings-held credentials

### Outputs / Evidence

- Handover pack v1.0, frozen read-only, at the repository root with dated table of contents
- Credential transfer sheet acknowledged by the client
- Spot-check record signed by Manoj

### Acceptance criteria

- Pack v1.0 frozen by 2026-11-19 with all listed contents present
- Ten-row spot check passes: every sampled row resolves to working evidence
- Credential transfer sheet complete and client-acknowledged
- Open-items log included with owners and dates

issues.name: Build 12-month ISMS operating calendar for the client
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Build a 12-month calendar of every recurring ISMS duty the client must keep running after Underwings leaves — this preserves ML3 established-and-practised maturity between assessments. Each entry carries duty, frequency, the responsible client role as trained in P4.3, and the evidence to file when done.

Populate from the procedures and exercise reports: quarterly access reviews (P3.1), monthly patch and vulnerability cycle (P3.6), semi-annual restore test (P3.5), log review (P3.4), supplier reassessment (P3.11), awareness refresh and phishing repeats (P4.4), annual incident and BC/DR exercises (P3.12, P3.13), internal audit programme (P4.5), management review, and document review dates from the P2.14 register. Add the external milestones: Stage 1 and Stage 2 from P5.4, the AL2 assessment from P5.3, and ISO surveillance roughly 12 months after certification.

Masha schedules around production peaks, Ramadan and Eid, UAE public holidays and plant shutdowns, confirming dates with the ISMS owner. Deliver as a monthly view plus a one-line what-who-evidence register, importable into the client's Outlook or 365 calendar. A named client-side calendar owner — normally the ISMS owner — accepts dates in writing; the calendar is walked in P5.9.

### Inputs

- Output of P4.3 (trained roles per recurring duty)
- Procedures and cadences from P3.1, P3.4, P3.5, P3.6, P3.11, P4.4, P4.5
- Booking dates from P5.3 and P5.4
- Client holiday and production calendar

### Outputs / Evidence

- 12-month ISMS operating calendar plus duty register, filed in the handover section
- Calendar import file
- Written date acceptance from the calendar owner

### Acceptance criteria

- Every recurring duty listed with role, frequency and evidence expectation
- External assessment milestones included
- Client-side calendar owner appointed and dates accepted in writing

issues.name: Deliver handover session; train client ISMS owner
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Half-day session on 09-24 with the ISMS owner, IT lead and sponsor — the formal transfer of ISMS operation to the client. Manoj delivers content; Masha runs logistics, materials and attendance.

First hour: walk the P5.7 pack — where everything lives, how the P0.7 tracker links controls to evidence, how the P2.14 register controls changes, how the P5.8 calendar drives the year. The ISMS owner drives the screen: they navigate, Manoj corrects. Spend extra time on weak spots from the P5.5 focus list.

Second hour: rehearse the external events day by day — Stage 1 (documentation review, readiness verdict, findings to clear before Stage 2), Stage 2 (interviews, sampling, shop-floor walk) and the TISAX AL2 remote plausibility interview against the P5.2 self-assessment. Cover conduct: who sits in each session, what evidence to have open, answer short and factual, never guess. Agree and minute Underwings attendance arrangements with the sponsor.

Close with Q&A, then sign the **handover acceptance form**: pack received, calendar accepted, roles understood, support arrangements agreed. That signature is the gate for P5.10 closure.

### Inputs

- Output of P5.7 (frozen handover pack) and P5.8 (accepted calendar)
- Output of P5.5 (focus list)
- Booking details from P5.3 and P5.4
- ISMS owner, IT lead and sponsor booked for a half day

### Outputs / Evidence

- Signed handover acceptance form, filed in the handover section
- Agenda, materials and attendance record

issues.name: Keep ISMS operating through assessment window (monthly evidence refresh)
issues.description_md:
### Guidance

Keep the ISMS demonstrably **operating** through the whole assessment window — the CB auditors and the TISAX assessor must see live operation, not a frozen snapshot from the delivery phase. This is a rolling task: run a monthly evidence refresh for each month of the window, following the 12-month operating calendar built in P5.8 and executed by the client role-holders trained in P4.3.

Each refresh, Masha collects and files: an access-review sample, a backup job record with a restore-check note, log-review notes with follow-ups, the incident log (entries or a documented nil-return), KPI capture against the P2.2 objectives, and minutes of any security meetings. Manoj signs the technical items.

Time the refreshes so evidence under 30 days old exists just before each external session (P6.2, P6.4, P6.6), and surface any missed cadence at the A-call check-ins — never in front of an auditor.

### Inputs

- 12-month operating calendar (P5.8) and named role-holders (P4.3)
- Evidence repository structure and conventions (P0.6)
- KPI definitions from the security objectives (P2.2)

### Outputs / Evidence

- Dated monthly refresh pack for each month of the assessment window
- Manoj sign-off on the technical items in every pack
- Exception notes for any missed cadence, with recovery action

### Acceptance criteria

- A complete refresh pack filed for every month of the assessment window
- Each pack contains all six item types or a documented nil-return
- Operating evidence under 30 days old available at each external audit session
- Misses raised at the next A-call with a recovery action and owner

Run the internal retrospective on Underwings' first combined through-certification delivery: what the re-baseline taught about phase lengths, procurement and booking lead times, and the assessment-window workload — feed the conclusions back into the house method. Present commercial follow-ons to the sponsor: surveillance-audit support and a continuous compliance subscription. Obtain the final acceptance sign-off.

### Inputs

- Follow-on proposal issued to the sponsor
